+# Dockerfile.ablation — container executor image for the cycle-130 component ablation
+# (SDD D-4.9 / DEC-0411). Extends Dockerfile.sandbox's pinned base and non-root user
+# with the Claude Code CLI, the codex CLI, pytest and bats. It holds NO credentials.
+# pipeline-run.sh mounts exactly two host paths: the sandbox read-write at /workspace
+# and a per-run writable HOME at /home/evaluser (<run>/meta/home: the codex CLI's
+# auth.json/config.toml copies, empty .claude/ and .aws/; the CLI's session store). The
+# Bedrock route authenticates from AWS_BEARER_TOKEN_BEDROCK passed in the environment.
+# The image's tool versions (below) are the batch's versions: every arm runs here.
+#
+# Build (no build context is needed; nothing is COPY'd):
+#   docker build -t loa-ablation:258 - < evals/harness/Dockerfile.ablation
+# Run:
+#   evals/harness/pipeline-run.sh --executor container --image loa-ablation:258 …
+#   (pipeline-run.sh passes --rm --name --user --network bridge --read-only --tmpfs /tmp
+#    --pids-limit 512 --memory 4g --cpus 2 and exactly the two mounts)
+#
+# Digest pinned 2026-02-11 (same base as Dockerfile.sandbox):
+#   docker manifest inspect node:20.11.0-bookworm-slim | jq '.manifests[0].digest'
+FROM rust:1-bookworm AS brbuild
+RUN cargo install beads_rust --version 0.2.6 --root /opt/br --locked 2>/dev/null || cargo install beads_rust --version 0.2.6 --root /opt/br
+
+FROM node:20.11.0-bookworm-slim@sha256:8ea90c4f037cc3c2f566eb46c53eaac005129113487eda4090058fe554578104 AS base
+
+ARG CLAUDE_CODE_VERSION=2.1.299
+ARG CODEX_VERSION=0.162.1
+ARG PYTEST_VERSION=9.0.2
+ARG BATS_VERSION=v1.13.0
+
+RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
+    bash \
+    git \
+    jq \
+    python3 \
+    python3-pip \
+    python3-venv \
+    grep \
+    diffutils \
+    coreutils \
+    procps \
+    ca-certificates \
+    curl \
+    && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*
+
+# yq (mikefarah/yq) with SHA256 integrity verification (as Dockerfile.sandbox)
+ARG YQ_VERSION=v4.40.5
+ARG YQ_SHA256_AMD64=0d6aaf1cf44a8d18fbc7ed0ef14f735a8df8d2e314c4cc0f0242d35c0a440c95
+ARG YQ_SHA256_ARM64=9431f0fa39a0af03a152d7fe19a86e42e9ff28d503ed4a70598f9261ec944a97
+RUN arch=$(dpkg --print-architecture) && \
+    case "$arch" in \
+      amd64) yq_arch="amd64"; yq_sha256="${YQ_SHA256_AMD64}" ;; \
+      arm64) yq_arch="arm64"; yq_sha256="${YQ_SHA256_ARM64}" ;; \
+      *) echo "Unsupported architecture: $arch" && exit 1 ;; \
+    esac && \
+    curl -fsSL "https://github.com/mikefarah/yq/releases/download/${YQ_VERSION}/yq_linux_${yq_arch}" \
+      -o /usr/local/bin/yq && \
+    echo "${yq_sha256}  /usr/local/bin/yq" | sha256sum -c - && \
+    chmod +x /usr/local/bin/yq
+
+# The two CLIs at the versions the fingerprint pins (exact versions, no ranges).
+RUN npm install -g --no-fund --no-audit \
+      "@anthropic-ai/claude-code@${CLAUDE_CODE_VERSION}" \
+      "@openai/codex@${CODEX_VERSION}" \
+    && npm cache clean --force
+
+# pytest for Python fixtures (bookworm's pip is externally managed)
+RUN pip3 install --no-cache-dir --break-system-packages "pytest==${PYTEST_VERSION}"
+# cheval's declared dependencies (.claude/adapters/pyproject.toml: dependencies + the `full` extra),
+# so the sandbox gates (adversarial-review.sh, flatline-orchestrator.sh) can dispatch (lead, DEC-0482)
+RUN pip3 install --no-cache-dir --break-system-packages "rfc8785>=0.1.4" "jsonschema>=4.21" "pyyaml>=6.0" "httpx[http2]>=0.24.0"
+
+# bats-core at the pinned tag
+RUN git clone --depth 1 --branch "${BATS_VERSION}" https://github.com/bats-core/bats-core.git /tmp/bats-core && \
+    /tmp/bats-core/install.sh /usr/local && \
+    rm -rf /tmp/bats-core
+
+# Disable npm lifecycle scripts for anything the agent installs later
+RUN npm config set ignore-scripts true
+
+# Non-root user (as Dockerfile.sandbox). At run time /home/evaluser is replaced by the
+# per-run HOME bind mount and the process runs as the host uid (--user).
+RUN groupadd -r evaluser && useradd -r -g evaluser -d /home/evaluser -s /bin/bash evaluser
+# No beads (br) in the image: beads_rust 0.2.6 is not on crates.io and the host binary needs glibc 2.38+; the sandbox
+# materialiser writes the beads opt-out marker (LOA_EVAL_BR_BIN unset/absent), so every arm runs the skills'
+# markdown fallback alike (lead, Sprint 258).
+RUN mkdir -p /home/evaluser/.aws /home/evaluser/.claude /home/evaluser/.codex /workspace && \
+    chown -R evaluser:evaluser /home/evaluser /workspace
+
+ENV TZ=UTC
+ENV LC_ALL=C
+ENV HOME=/home/evaluser
+ENV NPM_CONFIG_IGNORE_SCRIPTS=true
+ENV CLAUDE_CODE_USE_BEDROCK=1
+
+USER evaluser
+WORKDIR /workspace
+
+# Health check — every tool the fingerprint names is present
+RUN bash --version && git --version && jq --version && node --version && \
+    python3 --version && python3 -m pytest --version && yq --version && \
+    bats --version && claude --version && codex --version && \
+    echo "All tools verified"
+
+ENTRYPOINT []
+CMD ["/bin/bash"]

+# Dockerfile.ablation — container executor image for the cycle-130 component ablation
+# (SDD D-4.9 / DEC-0411). Extends Dockerfile.sandbox's pinned base and non-root user
+# with the Claude Code CLI, the codex CLI, pytest and bats. It holds NO credentials.
+# pipeline-run.sh mounts exactly two host paths: the sandbox read-write at /workspace
+# and a per-run writable HOME at /home/evaluser (<run>/meta/home: the codex CLI's
+# auth.json/config.toml copies, empty .claude/ and .aws/; the CLI's session store). The
+# Bedrock route authenticates from AWS_BEARER_TOKEN_BEDROCK passed in the environment.
+# The image's tool versions (below) are the batch's versions: every arm runs here.
+#
+# Build (no build context is needed; nothing is COPY'd):
+#   docker build -t loa-ablation:258 - < evals/harness/Dockerfile.ablation
+# Run:
+#   evals/harness/pipeline-run.sh --executor container --image loa-ablation:258 …
+#   (pipeline-run.sh passes --rm --name --user --network bridge --read-only --tmpfs /tmp
+#    --pids-limit 512 --memory 4g --cpus 2 and exactly the two mounts)
+#
+# Digest pinned 2026-02-11 (same base as Dockerfile.sandbox):
+#   docker manifest inspect node:20.11.0-bookworm-slim | jq '.manifests[0].digest'
+FROM rust:1-bookworm AS brbuild
+RUN cargo install beads_rust --version 0.2.6 --root /opt/br --locked 2>/dev/null || cargo install beads_rust --version 0.2.6 --root /opt/br
+
+FROM node:20.11.0-bookworm-slim@sha256:8ea90c4f037cc3c2f566eb46c53eaac005129113487eda4090058fe554578104 AS base
+
+ARG CLAUDE_CODE_VERSION=2.1.299
+ARG CODEX_VERSION=0.162.1
+ARG PYTEST_VERSION=9.0.2
+ARG BATS_VERSION=v1.13.0
+
+RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
+    bash \
+    git \
+    jq \
+    python3 \
+    python3-pip \
+    python3-venv \
+    grep \
+    diffutils \
+    coreutils \
+    procps \
+    ca-certificates \
+    curl \
+    && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*
+
+# yq (mikefarah/yq) with SHA256 integrity verification (as Dockerfile.sandbox)
+ARG YQ_VERSION=v4.40.5
+ARG YQ_SHA256_AMD64=0d6aaf1cf44a8d18fbc7ed0ef14f735a8df8d2e314c4cc0f0242d35c0a440c95
+ARG YQ_SHA256_ARM64=9431f0fa39a0af03a152d7fe19a86e42e9ff28d503ed4a70598f9261ec944a97
+RUN arch=$(dpkg --print-architecture) && \
+    case "$arch" in \
+      amd64) yq_arch="amd64"; yq_sha256="${YQ_SHA256_AMD64}" ;; \
+      arm64) yq_arch="arm64"; yq_sha256="${YQ_SHA256_ARM64}" ;; \
+      *) echo "Unsupported architecture: $arch" && exit 1 ;; \
+    esac && \
+    curl -fsSL "https://github.com/mikefarah/yq/releases/download/${YQ_VERSION}/yq_linux_${yq_arch}" \
+      -o /usr/local/bin/yq && \
+    echo "${yq_sha256}  /usr/local/bin/yq" | sha256sum -c - && \
+    chmod +x /usr/local/bin/yq
+
+# The two CLIs at the versions the fingerprint pins (exact versions, no ranges).
+RUN npm install -g --no-fund --no-audit \
+      "@anthropic-ai/claude-code@${CLAUDE_CODE_VERSION}" \
+      "@openai/codex@${CODEX_VERSION}" \
+    && npm cache clean --force
+
+# pytest for Python fixtures (bookworm's pip is externally managed)
+RUN pip3 install --no-cache-dir --break-system-packages "pytest==${PYTEST_VERSION}"
+# cheval's declared dependencies (.claude/adapters/pyproject.toml: dependencies + the `full` extra),
+# so the sandbox gates (adversarial-review.sh, flatline-orchestrator.sh) can dispatch (lead, DEC-0482)
+RUN pip3 install --no-cache-dir --break-system-packages "rfc8785>=0.1.4" "jsonschema>=4.21" "pyyaml>=6.0" "httpx[http2]>=0.24.0"
+
+# bats-core at the pinned tag
+RUN git clone --depth 1 --branch "${BATS_VERSION}" https://github.com/bats-core/bats-core.git /tmp/bats-core && \
+    /tmp/bats-core/install.sh /usr/local && \
+    rm -rf /tmp/bats-core
+
+# Disable npm lifecycle scripts for anything the agent installs later
+RUN npm config set ignore-scripts true
+
+# Non-root user (as Dockerfile.sandbox). At run time /home/evaluser is replaced by the
+# per-run HOME bind mount and the process runs as the host uid (--user).
+RUN groupadd -r evaluser && useradd -r -g evaluser -d /home/evaluser -s /bin/bash evaluser
+# No beads (br) in the image: beads_rust 0.2.6 is not on crates.io and the host binary needs glibc 2.38+; the sandbox
+# materialiser writes the beads opt-out marker (LOA_EVAL_BR_BIN unset/absent), so every arm runs the skills'
+# markdown fallback alike (lead, Sprint 258).
+RUN mkdir -p /home/evaluser/.aws /home/evaluser/.claude /home/evaluser/.codex /workspace && \
+    chown -R evaluser:evaluser /home/evaluser /workspace
+
+ENV TZ=UTC
+ENV LC_ALL=C
+ENV HOME=/home/evaluser
+ENV NPM_CONFIG_IGNORE_SCRIPTS=true
+ENV CLAUDE_CODE_USE_BEDROCK=1
+
+USER evaluser
+WORKDIR /workspace
+
+# Health check — every tool the fingerprint names is present
+RUN bash --version && git --version && jq --version && node --version && \
+    python3 --version && python3 -m pytest --version && yq --version && \
+    bats --version && claude --version && codex --version && \
+    echo "All tools verified"
+
+ENTRYPOINT []
+CMD ["/bin/bash"]

# cycle-102 Sprint 1 T1.9: reasoning-class /v1/responses (closes A1).
        max_output_tokens: 32000
        # cycle-102 Sprint 1F: parity with gpt-5.5-pro input-size gate. Same
        # cheval HTTP-asymmetry failure mode (KF-002 layer 3).
        # Sprint 4A (cycle-102, AC-4.5e): streaming transport now defaults
        # on for openai_adapter._complete_streaming, eliminating the 60s
        # server-side disconnect class by construction. The gate stays as
        # belt-and-suspenders against future intermediary-timer regressions
        # AND against context-window overflow (well below 400K). Raised
        # from 24000 → 200000 to reflect streaming's actual safe range.
        # Operator override per-call: `--max-input-tokens N` (0 disables);
        # global: `LOA_CHEVAL_DISABLE_INPUT_GATE=1`. Kill streaming via
        # `LOA_CHEVAL_DISABLE_STREAMING=1` to fall back to the legacy
        # non-streaming path (which still hits the original 24K wall).
        # cycle-103 Sprint 3 T3.4 / AC-3.4: split into streaming-default
        # vs legacy-fallback. When `LOA_CHEVAL_DISABLE_STREAMING=1`, the
        # gate uses `legacy_max_input_tokens` automatically — operator no
        # longer has to manually lower the cap after killing streaming.
        max_input_tokens: 200000          # backward-compat fallback
        streaming_max_input_tokens: 200000
        legacy_max_input_tokens: 24000    # pre-Sprint-4A KF-002 wall
        # cycle-095 Sprint 2: probe_required dropped — gpt-5.5 is GA on /v1/models
        # since 2026-04-23. Probe-gated fail-fast still applies via the
        # generic AVAILABLE/UNAVAILABLE state in .run/model-health-cache.json
        # (see PRD G-7 + Sprint 1 probe_required clarification block in sprint.md).
        # Wire-protocol gate: OpenAI's Responses API for gpt-5.5 rejects the
        # `temperature` parameter with HTTP 400 ("Unsupported parameter:
        # 'temperature' is not supported with this model"). The cheval adapter
        # at .claude/adapters/loa_cheval/providers/openai_adapter.py consults
        # `params.temperature_supported` per request and omits the field when
        # False (mirrors the claude-opus-4-7 #641 pattern). Verified
        # 2026-05-07 via direct curl to /v1/responses.
        params:
          temperature_supported: false
        pricing:
          input_per_mtok: 5000000       # $5.00 per million tokens (confirmed 2026-04-29)
          output_per_mtok: 30000000     # $30.00 per million tokens (output_tokens INCLUSIVE of reasoning_tokens; SDD §5.5)
      gpt-6.1-sol:
        # cycle-130 Sprint 258 (2026-10-15): the model Codex on a ChatGPT plan
        # serves by default after it withdrew every gpt-5.x name (KF-044); the
        # codex-headless hop's cli_model points here so its estimates price
        # through this entry. Listed by /v1/models with the operator's key.
        # Shape mirrored from gpt-5.5 (400K window, /v1/responses, 32K out).
        auth_type: http_api
        dispatch_group: openai-gpt
        capabilities: [chat, tools, function_calling, code]
        context_window: 400000
        token_param: max_completion_tokens
        # within-company chain, terminating in the CLI hop as every OpenAI primary does
        fallback_chain:
          - openai:codex-headless
        endpoint_family: responses
        max_output_tokens: 32000
        max_input_tokens: 200000
        streaming_max_input_tokens: 200000
        legacy_max_input_tokens: 24000
        params:
          temperature_supported: false
        pricing:
          # PLACEHOLDER: gpt-5.5 list prices copied 2026-10-15 until the gpt-6.1
          # rate card is confirmed (bead at the Sprint 258 close). The codex
          # hop itself bills the operator's subscription; this entry prices
          # estimates and MODELINV rows only.
          input_per_mtok: 5000000       # $5.00 per million tokens (placeholder, see above)
          output_per_mtok: 30000000     # $30.00 per million tokens (placeholder, see above)
      gpt-5.5-pro:
        # cycle-110 sprint-2a T2.3 (SDD §3.2): auth_type + dispatch_group migration.
        auth_type: http_api
        dispatch_group: openai-gpt
        capabilities: [chat, tools, function_calling, code]
        context_window: 400000
        token_param: max_completion_tokens
        # cycle-104 Sprint 2 T2.3: load-bearing chain — KF-003 absorption.
        # Within-company ONLY. Empty-content on gpt-5.5-pro walks to
        # gpt-5.5 → gpt-5.3-codex → codex-headless (CLI bypass). No
        # cross-company entry (G1 — 3-company BB diversity).
      codex-headless:
        # cycle-110 sprint-2a T2.3 (SDD §3.2): auth_type + dispatch_group migration.
        auth_type: headless
        dispatch_group: openai-gpt
        kind: cli                       # NEW field — distinguishes HTTP vs CLI
        capabilities: [chat, code]      # No tools, no structured_json
        # #881 close, #914 F-001 correction: declare the real per-CLI context
        # window so cheval's enforce_context_window does not pull the 128000-
        # token global default (loa_cheval/types.py:107). The codex CLI
        # dispatches gpt-5.5 by default — matches the http_api gpt-5.5 entry
        # in this file (context_window: 400000). The initial PR shipped
        # 200000 with an inaccurate comment claiming gpt-5.5 was 200000;
        # corrected post-BB review to the real 400000 capacity.
        context_window: 400000
        # No pricing entry — CLI uses operator's Codex subscription.
        # cycle-104 sprint-2 T2.11 amendment: cli_model is the model
        # passed to `codex exec --model <name>`. The CLI doesn't
        # recognize the Loa alias; this maps to the real codex model.
        # cycle-130 Sprint 258 (2026-10-15): Codex on a ChatGPT plan no longer
        # serves any gpt-5.x name (HTTP 400 "not supported when using Codex
        # with a ChatGPT account" for gpt-5.5, gpt-5.5-pro, gpt-5.5-codex,
        # gpt-5.3-codex; codex 0.137 and 0.162 alike). The CLI's own default
        # is gpt-6.1-sol, which answers; the HTTP gpt-5.5 entries above are
        # unchanged (the API still lists them). Recorded as KF-044.
        extra:
          cli_model: gpt-6.1-sol

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
     2	# Loa Framework: CI/CD Validation (Enterprise Grade)
     3	# v0.9.0 Lossless Ledger Protocol - Enhanced validation
     4	# Exit codes: 0 = success, 1 = failure
     5	set -euo pipefail
     6	
     7	
     8	# sprint-bug-172 / bug-911: sha256_portable from compat-lib
     9	source "$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)/compat-lib.sh"
    10	
    11	VERSION_FILE=".loa-version.json"
    12	CHECKSUMS_FILE=".claude/checksums.json"
    13	CONFIG_FILE=".loa.config.yaml"
    14	NOTES_FILE="grimoires/loa/NOTES.md"
    15	
    16	# v0.9.0 Protocol files
    17	PROTOCOL_DIR=".claude/protocols"
    18	SCRIPT_DIR=".claude/scripts"
    19	# bug 20260922-13a3d1: single Aleph opt-in predicate (missing lib → disabled).
    20	if [[ -f "${SCRIPT_DIR}/lib/aleph-opt-in.sh" ]]; then
    21	  # shellcheck source=lib/aleph-opt-in.sh
    22	  source "${SCRIPT_DIR}/lib/aleph-opt-in.sh"
    23	else
    24	  aleph_opt_in_enabled() { return 1; }
    25	fi
    26	
    27	# Disable colors in CI or non-interactive mode
    28	if [[ "${CI:-}" == "true" ]] || [[ ! -t 1 ]]; then
    29	  RED=''; GREEN=''; YELLOW=''; NC=''
    30	else
    31	  RED='\033[0;31m'; GREEN='\033[0;32m'; YELLOW='\033[1;33m'; NC='\033[0m'
    32	fi
    33	
    34	log() { echo -e "${GREEN}[loa-check]${NC} $*"; }
    35	warn() { echo -e "${YELLOW}[loa-check]${NC} $*"; }
    36	fail() { echo -e "${RED}[loa-check]${NC} x $*"; FAILURES=$((FAILURES + 1)); }
    37	
    38	FAILURES=0

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
     2	# =============================================================================
     3	# tools/gen-checksums.sh — cycle-130 FR-1 (#1267; SDD §5.1, DEC-0368)
     4	#
     5	# Writes the System Zone integrity manifest `.claude/checksums.json` from the
     6	# TRACKED `.claude/` tree only. The legacy generators (mount-loa.sh and
     7	# update.sh `generate_checksums`) walk the working tree with `find`, so build,
     8	# cache and runtime artefacts (`__pycache__`, `.pytest_cache`, `node_modules`,
     9	# `.run/`) that exist only on the generating machine end up in the manifest and
    10	# read as Missing on every fresh mount. This generator lists
    11	#
    12	#   git -C ROOT ls-files -z -- .claude
    13	#
    14	# minus every path under `.claude/overrides/` (user-owned) and minus the
    15	# manifest itself (`.claude/checksums.json`), hashes each with
    16	# `sha256_portable` (.claude/scripts/compat-lib.sh) and writes
    17	#
    18	#   {"generated": "<UTC ISO-8601>", "algorithm": "sha256",
    19	#    "files": {"<path>": "<sha256 hex>", ...}}
    20	#
    21	# pretty-printed by jq (2-space), keys in `LC_ALL=C` byte order. Two runs on
    22	# the same tree are byte-identical except `generated`. The working-tree content
    23	# of each tracked path is hashed (an unstaged edit is reflected); a tracked
    24	# path deleted from the working tree is skipped with a warning on stderr.
    25	#
    26	# Usage:
    27	#   tools/gen-checksums.sh [--root DIR] [--out FILE]   # (re)generate
    28	#   tools/gen-checksums.sh --check [--root DIR] [--out FILE]
    29	#
    30	# Options:
    31	#   --root DIR   repository work tree to read (default: the git top level of
    32	#                the current directory)
    33	#   --out FILE   manifest path (default: ROOT/.claude/checksums.json). With
    34	#                --check this is the committed manifest that is compared.
    35	#   --check      regenerate to a temp file and compare its `files` map with
    36	#                the manifest at --out; nothing is written
    37	#   -h, --help   this text
    38	#
    39	# Exit codes:
    40	#   0  generated, or --check: the `files` maps are identical
    41	#   1  --check: drift (the first ten differing paths, each labelled added /
    42	#      removed / changed, on stderr) or the manifest is absent / not JSON
    43	#   2  usage error, ROOT is not a git work tree, or a tracked path name that
    44	#      cannot be represented safely (newline, tab or backslash)
    45	# =============================================================================
    46	set -euo pipefail
    47	export LC_ALL=C
    48	
    49	SELF_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
    50	# shellcheck source=../.claude/scripts/compat-lib.sh
    51	source "${SELF_DIR}/../.claude/scripts/compat-lib.sh"
    52	
    53	usage() { sed -n '/^# Usage:/,/^# =====/p' "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}" | sed -e '$d' -e 's/^# \{0,1\}//'; }
    54	die2() { echo "gen-checksums: $*" >&2; exit 2; }
    55	
    56	MANIFEST_REL=".claude/checksums.json"
    57	ROOT=""
    58	OUT=""
    59	CHECK=0
    60	while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
    61	  case "$1" in
    62	    --check) CHECK=1; shift ;;
    63	    --root)
    64	      [[ $# -ge 2 && -n "$2" ]] || die2 "--root requires a directory"
    65	      ROOT="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    66	    --out)
    67	      [[ $# -ge 2 && -n "$2" ]] || die2 "--out requires a file path"
    68	      OUT="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    69	    -h|--help) usage; exit 0 ;;
    70	    *) die2 "unknown argument: $1 (see --help)" ;;
    71	  esac
    72	done
    73	
    74	if [[ -z "$ROOT" ]]; then
    75	  ROOT="$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel 2>/dev/null)" || die2 "not inside a git work tree (use --root DIR)"
    76	fi
    77	[[ -d "$ROOT" ]] || die2 "--root is not a directory: $ROOT"
    78	ROOT="$(cd "$ROOT" && pwd -P)"
    79	[[ "$(git -C "$ROOT" rev-parse --is-inside-work-tree 2>/dev/null || true)" == "true" ]] \
    80	  || die2 "not a git work tree: $ROOT"
    81	[[ -n "$OUT" ]] || OUT="${ROOT}/${MANIFEST_REL}"
    82	
    83	TMP_DIR="$(mktemp -d "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/gen-checksums.XXXXXX")"
    84	cleanup() { rm -rf "$TMP_DIR"; }
    85	trap cleanup EXIT
    86	
    87	# --- 1. the tracked set (NUL-safe, C-sorted, overrides and manifest removed) --
    88	files=()
    89	while IFS= read -r -d '' path; do
    90	  case "$path" in
    91	    .claude/overrides/*|"$MANIFEST_REL") continue ;;
    92	  esac
    93	  case "$path" in
    94	    *$'\n'*|*$'\t'*|*\\*) die2 "refusing a tracked path with a newline, tab or backslash: $(printf '%q' "$path")" ;;
    95	  esac
    96	  if [[ ! -f "${ROOT}/${path}" ]]; then
    97	    # A gitlink, a dangling symlink or a path deleted in the working tree.
    98	    echo "gen-checksums: warning: tracked path not a file in the working tree, skipped: $path" >&2
    99	    continue
   100	  fi
   101	  files+=("$path")
   102	done < <(git -C "$ROOT" ls-files -z -- .claude | sort -z)
   103	
   104	# --- 2. hash in chunks (one sha256 process per 400 paths, order preserved) ----
   105	TSV="${TMP_DIR}/files.tsv"
   106	: > "$TSV"

   169	#!/usr/bin/env bash

   171	# tools/check-manifest-paths.sh — cycle-130 FR-1 (#1267; SDD §5.2, DEC-0368)
   172	#
   173	# CI gate for the System Zone integrity manifest: every path listed in
   174	# `.claude/checksums.json` must be TRACKED (`git ls-files -- .claude`) and
   175	# PRESENT in the working tree. A manifest generated by walking a dirty tree
   176	# (the #1267 class) lists build, cache and runtime artefacts that no fresh
   177	# mount has, so every downstream `check-loa.sh` reports them as Missing.
   178	#
   179	# Offenders are grouped on stderr:
   180	#   untracked  — listed in the manifest, not in `git ls-files`; each carries a
   181	#                DIAGNOSTIC class (first match wins):
   182	#                  __pycache__ | .pytest_cache | node_modules | .run
   183	#                      (a path component of that name)
   184	#                  .pyc   (name ends in .pyc)
   185	#                  .lock  (name ends in .lock)
   186	#                  other
   187	#   missing    — tracked, but absent from the working tree
   188	# The classes label untracked offenders only: a TRACKED path is never flagged
   189	# for its name (a committed `.lock` fixture is legitimate).
   190	#
   191	# Last line on stdout:
   192	#   manifest-paths: N entries, M untracked (class=count, ...), K missing
   193	#
   194	# Usage:
   195	#   tools/check-manifest-paths.sh [--manifest FILE] [--root DIR]
   196	#
   197	# Options:
   198	#   --root DIR       repository work tree (default: the git top level of the
   199	#                    current directory)
   200	#   --manifest FILE  manifest to check (default: ROOT/.claude/checksums.json)
   201	#   -h, --help       this text
   202	#
   203	# Exit codes:
   204	#   0  every manifest path is tracked and present
   205	#   1  at least one untracked or missing path (listed on stderr)
   206	#   2  usage error, ROOT is not a git work tree, or the manifest is absent or
   207	#      not JSON with a `files` object
   208	# =============================================================================
   209	set -euo pipefail
   210	export LC_ALL=C
   211	
   212	usage() { sed -n '/^# Usage:/,/^# =====/p' "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}" | sed -e '$d' -e 's/^# \{0,1\}//'; }
   213	die2() { echo "check-manifest-paths: $*" >&2; exit 2; }
   214	
   215	ROOT=""
   216	MANIFEST=""
   217	while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
   218	  case "$1" in
   219	    --root)
   220	      [[ $# -ge 2 && -n "$2" ]] || die2 "--root requires a directory"
   221	      ROOT="$2"; shift 2 ;;
   222	    --manifest)
   223	      [[ $# -ge 2 && -n "$2" ]] || die2 "--manifest requires a file path"
   224	      MANIFEST="$2"; shift 2 ;;
   225	    -h|--help) usage; exit 0 ;;
   226	    *) die2 "unknown argument: $1 (see --help)" ;;
   227	  esac
   228	done
   229	
   230	if [[ -z "$ROOT" ]]; then
   231	  ROOT="$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel 2>/dev/null)" || die2 "not inside a git work tree (use --root DIR)"
   232	fi
   233	[[ -d "$ROOT" ]] || die2 "--root is not a directory: $ROOT"

   235	[[ "$(git -C "$ROOT" rev-parse --is-inside-work-tree 2>/dev/null || true)" == "true" ]] \
   236	  || die2 "not a git work tree: $ROOT"
   237	[[ -n "$MANIFEST" ]] || MANIFEST="${ROOT}/.claude/checksums.json"
   238	[[ -f "$MANIFEST" ]] || die2 "manifest not found: $MANIFEST"

   240	  || die2 "manifest is not JSON with a files object: $MANIFEST"
   241	
   242	TMP_DIR="$(mktemp -d "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/check-manifest-paths.XXXXXX")"
   243	cleanup() { rm -rf "$TMP_DIR"; }
   244	trap cleanup EXIT
   245	
   246	# Both lists newline-separated and C-sorted. A path with a newline cannot be
   247	# represented in either list; gen-checksums.sh refuses to emit one.
   248	git -C "$ROOT" ls-files -- .claude | sort -u > "${TMP_DIR}/tracked"
   249	jq -r '.files | keys[]' "$MANIFEST" | sort -u > "${TMP_DIR}/listed"
   250	comm -23 "${TMP_DIR}/listed" "${TMP_DIR}/tracked" > "${TMP_DIR}/untracked"
   251	comm -12 "${TMP_DIR}/listed" "${TMP_DIR}/tracked" > "${TMP_DIR}/both"
   252	
   253	classify() {
   254	  local p="$1"
   255	  if [[ "$p" =~ (^|/)(__pycache__|\.pytest_cache|node_modules|\.run)(/|$) ]]; then
   256	    printf '%s' "${BASH_REMATCH[2]}"

   261	  else
   262	    printf 'other'
   263	  fi
   264	}

   268	while IFS= read -r p; do
   269	  [[ -n "$p" ]] || continue
   270	  printf '%s\t%s\n' "$(classify "$p")" "$p" >> "${TMP_DIR}/untracked.cls"
   271	done < "${TMP_DIR}/untracked"
   272	
   273	: > "${TMP_DIR}/missing"
   274	while IFS= read -r p; do
   275	  [[ -n "$p" ]] || continue
   276	  [[ -e "${ROOT}/${p}" ]] || printf '%s\n' "$p" >> "${TMP_DIR}/missing"
   277	done < "${TMP_DIR}/both"
   278	
   279	entries=$(wc -l < "${TMP_DIR}/listed" | tr -d ' ')
   280	n_untracked=$(wc -l < "${TMP_DIR}/untracked.cls" | tr -d ' ')
   281	n_missing=$(wc -l < "${TMP_DIR}/missing" | tr -d ' ')
   282	
   283	class_summary=""
   284	if [[ "$n_untracked" -gt 0 ]]; then
   285	  echo "check-manifest-paths: untracked manifest paths (not in git ls-files -- .claude), by class:" >&2

   288	    [[ "$c" -gt 0 ]] || continue
   289	    class_summary="${class_summary:+${class_summary}, }${cls}=${c}"
   290	    echo "  [${cls}] ${c} path(s):" >&2
   291	    awk -F'\t' -v c="$cls" '$1 == c { print "    " $2 }' "${TMP_DIR}/untracked.cls" >&2
   292	  done
   293	fi
   294	if [[ "$n_missing" -gt 0 ]]; then
   295	  echo "check-manifest-paths: tracked manifest paths absent from the working tree:" >&2
   296	  sed 's/^/    /' "${TMP_DIR}/missing" >&2
   297	fi

   299	echo "manifest-paths: ${entries} entries, ${n_untracked} untracked${class_summary:+ (${class_summary})}, ${n_missing} missing"

   301	  echo "check-manifest-paths: FAIL — regenerate with: bash tools/gen-checksums.sh" >&2
   302	  exit 1
   303	fi
   304	exit 0

   241	
   242	TMP_DIR="$(mktemp -d "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/check-manifest-paths.XXXXXX")"
   243	cleanup() { rm -rf "$TMP_DIR"; }
   244	trap cleanup EXIT
   245	
   246	# Both lists newline-separated and C-sorted. A path with a newline cannot be
   247	# represented in either list; gen-checksums.sh refuses to emit one.
   248	git -C "$ROOT" ls-files -- .claude | sort -u > "${TMP_DIR}/tracked"
   249	jq -r '.files | keys[]' "$MANIFEST" | sort -u > "${TMP_DIR}/listed"
   250	comm -23 "${TMP_DIR}/listed" "${TMP_DIR}/tracked" > "${TMP_DIR}/untracked"
   251	comm -12 "${TMP_DIR}/listed" "${TMP_DIR}/tracked" > "${TMP_DIR}/both"
   252	
   253	classify() {
   254	  local p="$1"
   255	  if [[ "$p" =~ (^|/)(__pycache__|\.pytest_cache|node_modules|\.run)(/|$) ]]; then
   256	    printf '%s' "${BASH_REMATCH[2]}"
   257	  elif [[ "$p" == *.pyc ]]; then
   258	    printf '.pyc'
   259	  elif [[ "$p" == *.lock ]]; then
   260	    printf '.lock'
   261	  else
   262	    printf 'other'
   263	  fi
   264	}
   265	
   266	# Classified untracked offenders: "<class>\t<path>"
   267	: > "${TMP_DIR}/untracked.cls"
   268	while IFS= read -r p; do
   269	  [[ -n "$p" ]] || continue
   270	  printf '%s\t%s\n' "$(classify "$p")" "$p" >> "${TMP_DIR}/untracked.cls"
   271	done < "${TMP_DIR}/untracked"
   272	
   273	: > "${TMP_DIR}/missing"
   274	while IFS= read -r p; do
   275	  [[ -n "$p" ]] || continue
   276	  [[ -e "${ROOT}/${p}" ]] || printf '%s\n' "$p" >> "${TMP_DIR}/missing"
   277	done < "${TMP_DIR}/both"
   278	
   279	entries=$(wc -l < "${TMP_DIR}/listed" | tr -d ' ')
   280	n_untracked=$(wc -l < "${TMP_DIR}/untracked.cls" | tr -d ' ')
   281	n_missing=$(wc -l < "${TMP_DIR}/missing" | tr -d ' ')
   282	
   283	class_summary=""
   284	if [[ "$n_untracked" -gt 0 ]]; then
   285	  echo "check-manifest-paths: untracked manifest paths (not in git ls-files -- .claude), by class:" >&2
   286	  for cls in __pycache__ .pytest_cache node_modules .run .pyc .lock other; do
   287	    c=$(awk -F'\t' -v c="$cls" '$1 == c' "${TMP_DIR}/untracked.cls" | wc -l | tr -d ' ')
   288	    [[ "$c" -gt 0 ]] || continue
   289	    class_summary="${class_summary:+${class_summary}, }${cls}=${c}"
   290	    echo "  [${cls}] ${c} path(s):" >&2
   291	    awk -F'\t' -v c="$cls" '$1 == c { print "    " $2 }' "${TMP_DIR}/untracked.cls" >&2
   292	  done
   293	fi
   294	if [[ "$n_missing" -gt 0 ]]; then
   295	  echo "check-manifest-paths: tracked manifest paths absent from the working tree:" >&2
   296	  sed 's/^/    /' "${TMP_DIR}/missing" >&2
   297	fi
   298	
   299	echo "manifest-paths: ${entries} entries, ${n_untracked} untracked${class_summary:+ (${class_summary})}, ${n_missing} missing"
   300	if [[ "$n_untracked" -gt 0 || "$n_missing" -gt 0 ]]; then
   301	  echo "check-manifest-paths: FAIL — regenerate with: bash tools/gen-checksums.sh" >&2
   302	  exit 1
   303	fi
   304	exit 0

    77	# on the source line), as eval.yml's trust-boundary scan requires.
    78	#
    79	# Evidence: every function reports `key=value` lines (one line, no newline in
    80	# the value). When ARM_EVIDENCE_FILE is set they are appended to that file;
    81	# else they go to the descriptor in SANDBOX_MOUNT_EVIDENCE_FD (default 1).
    82	# resolve_arm_toggles prints JSON on stdout and no evidence.

    87	
    88	[[ "${_SANDBOX_MOUNT_LOADED:-}" == "true" ]] && return 0

    90	
    91	_SM_LIB_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
    92	_SM_REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$_SM_LIB_DIR/../../.." && pwd)"
    93	
    94	_sm_err() { echo "ERROR: $*" >&2; }
    95	
    96	# _sm_sha256 <file>... prints "<hex>  <file>" lines, the sha256sum output shape.
    97	# Python hashlib, not compat-lib's sha256_portable: the eval workflow runs the
    98	# harness as the trusted copy against a PR's .claude/, so no harness script
    99	# sources .claude/ code (eval.yml "Validate grader trust boundary"); run-arms.sh
   100	# hashes the corpus the same way.
   101	_sm_sha256() {
   102	  python3 -I -c '
   103	import hashlib, sys
   104	for p in sys.argv[1:]:
   105	    h = hashlib.sha256()
   106	    with open(p, "rb") as f:
   107	        for b in iter(lambda: f.read(1 << 20), b""):
   108	            h.update(b)
   109	    print(h.hexdigest() + "  " + p)' "$@"
   110	}
   111	
   112	# _sm_evidence <key> <value> — one key=value line to the evidence sink.
   113	_sm_evidence() {
   114	  local line="$1=${2//$'\n'/ }"
   115	  if [[ -n "${ARM_EVIDENCE_FILE:-}" ]]; then
   116	    printf '%s\n' "$line" >> "$ARM_EVIDENCE_FILE"
   117	  else
   118	    local fd="${SANDBOX_MOUNT_EVIDENCE_FD:-1}"
   119	    [[ "$fd" =~ ^[0-9]$ ]] || fd=1
   120	    printf '%s\n' "$line" >&"$fd"
   121	  fi
   122	}
   123	
   124	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   125	mount_prompt_surface() {
   126	  local ws="$1" tree="$2" skill="${3:-}"
   127	  [[ -d "$ws" ]] || { _sm_err "mount_prompt_surface: workspace not found: $ws"; return 2; }
   128	  [[ -d "$tree/.claude" ]] || { _sm_err "mount_prompt_surface: prompt tree has no .claude/: $tree"; return 2; }
   129	  if [[ "$skill" == "-" ]]; then
   130	    mkdir -p "$ws/.claude"
   131	    cp -a "$tree/.claude/." "$ws/.claude/" || { _sm_err "mount_prompt_surface: copying .claude/ failed"; return 2; }
   132	    printf '@.claude/loa/CLAUDE.loa.md\n' > "$ws/CLAUDE.md"
   133	    if [[ -f "$tree/.loa.config.yaml" ]]; then cp "$tree/.loa.config.yaml" "$ws/.loa.config.yaml"; fi
   134	    _sm_evidence mount "tree"
   135	    return 0
   136	  fi
   137	  case "$skill" in */*|.*|'') _sm_err "invalid skill name '$skill'"; return 2 ;; esac
   138	  local skill_src="$tree/.claude/skills/$skill"
   139	  [[ -f "$skill_src/SKILL.md" ]] || { _sm_err "prompt tree $tree has no .claude/skills/$skill/SKILL.md"; return 2; }
   140	  mkdir -p "$ws/.claude/skills" "$ws/.claude/loa"
   141	  # Whole skill dir (resources included) so guarded reads inside the skill resolve.
   142	  local skill_dst="$ws/.claude/skills/$skill"
   143	  mkdir -p "$skill_dst"
   144	  cp -a "$skill_src/." "$skill_dst/"
   145	  if [[ -f "$tree/.claude/loa/CLAUDE.loa.md" ]]; then
   146	    cp "$tree/.claude/loa/CLAUDE.loa.md" "$ws/.claude/loa/CLAUDE.loa.md"
   147	  fi
   148	  if [[ -d "$tree/.claude/rules" ]]; then
   149	    mkdir -p "$ws/.claude/rules"
   150	    cp -a "$tree/.claude/rules/." "$ws/.claude/rules/"
   151	  fi
   152	  printf '@.claude/loa/CLAUDE.loa.md\n' > "$ws/CLAUDE.md"
   153	  if [[ -n "${LOA_EVAL_ARM+x}" && -f "$tree/.loa.config.yaml" ]]; then
   154	    cp "$tree/.loa.config.yaml" "$ws/.loa.config.yaml"
   155	  fi
   156	  _sm_evidence mount "skill:$skill"
   157	  return 0
   158	}
   159	
   160	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   161	resolve_arm_toggles() {
   162	  local arm="$1" suite_file="${2:-}"
   163	  [[ "$arm" =~ ^[a-z][a-z0-9_]{0,63}$ ]] || { _sm_err "invalid arm id '$arm'"; return 2; }
   164	  local found=0 entry=""
   165	  if [[ -n "$suite_file" && -f "$suite_file" ]]; then
   166	    # an unreadable suite file reads as "not declared" (cycle-129 behaviour: baseline still resolves to {})
   167	    entry="$(ARM="$arm" yq -o=json -I=0 '[((.arms // [])[]), ((.ab.arms // [])[])] | map(select(.id == strenv(ARM))) | .[0] // null' "$suite_file" 2>/dev/null)" \
   168	      || entry=""
   169	    [[ -n "$entry" && "$entry" != "null" ]] && found=1
   170	  fi
   171	  if [[ "$found" -eq 0 ]]; then
   172	    [[ "$arm" == "baseline" ]] && { printf '{}'; return 0; }
   173	    _sm_err "arm '$arm' is not declared in ${suite_file:-any suite} (arms[] / ab.arms[])"
   174	    return 2
   175	  fi
   176	  if [[ "$(jq -r '.absent // false' <<<"$entry")" == "true" ]]; then
   177	    _sm_err "arm '$arm' is declared absent in $suite_file (never run): $(jq -r '.evidence // "no evidence"' <<<"$entry")"
   178	    return 2
   179	  fi
   180	  local t
   181	  t="$(jq -c '.toggles // {}' <<<"$entry")"
   182	  jq -e 'type == "object"' >/dev/null 2>&1 <<<"$t" || { _sm_err "arm '$arm' toggles are not an object in $suite_file"; return 2; }
   183	  printf '%s' "$t"
   184	}
   185	
   186	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   187	# Remove the markdown section that starts at the exact heading line $2 (up to
   188	# the next level-2 heading) from file $1. Prints the number of lines removed.
   189	_sm_drop_md_section() {
   190	  local f="$1" heading="$2" tmpdir="$3" tmp
   191	  tmp="$(mktemp "$tmpdir/.arm.XXXXXX")"
   192	  awk -v h="$heading" '
   193	    $0 == h { skip = 1; n++; next }
   194	    skip && /^## / { skip = 0 }
   195	    skip { n++; next }
   196	    { print }
   197	    END { print n + 0 > "/dev/stderr" }' "$f" > "$tmp" 2> "$tmp.n"
   198	  mv "$tmp" "$f"
   199	  cat "$tmp.n"; rm -f "$tmp.n"
   200	}
   201	
   202	# Remove the first blank-line-delimited paragraph of $1 that contains one of
   203	# the needles (tried in order, case-insensitive). Writes the removed text to
   204	# $2; exit 1 when no needle matches.
   205	_sm_drop_paragraph() {
   206	  python3 -I - "$1" "$2" "look for what the review did not" "Confirm the review's demotions independently" <<'PY'
   207	import re, sys
   208	path, out = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2]
   209	text = open(path, encoding="utf-8").read()
   210	paras = re.split(r"(\n[ \t]*\n)", text)
   211	for needle in sys.argv[3:]:
   212	    for i in range(0, len(paras), 2):
   213	        if needle.lower() in paras[i].lower():
   214	            removed = paras[i]
   215	            # drop the paragraph and the separator that follows it
   216	            del paras[i:i + 2]
   217	            open(path, "w", encoding="utf-8").write("".join(paras))
   218	            open(out, "w", encoding="utf-8").write(removed + "\n")
   219	            sys.exit(0)
   220	sys.exit(1)
   221	PY
   222	}
   223	
   224	# Strip every `effort:` line from the YAML frontmatter of file $1 (frontmatter
   225	# = line 1 `---` up to the next `---`). Prints 1 when a line was removed, else 0.
   226	_sm_strip_frontmatter_effort() {
   227	  local f="$1" tmp
   228	  tmp="$(mktemp "$f.XXXXXX")"
   229	  awk '
   230	    NR == 1 && $0 == "---" { fm = 1; print; next }
   231	    fm == 1 && $0 == "---" { fm = 2; print; next }
   232	    fm == 1 && /^effort:/ { n++; next }
   233	    { print }
   234	    END { print (n > 0 ? 1 : 0) > "/dev/stderr" }' "$f" > "$tmp" 2> "$tmp.n"
   235	  cat "$tmp" > "$f"; rm -f "$tmp"
   236	  cat "$tmp.n"; rm -f "$tmp.n"
   237	}
   238	
   239	# 0 when file $1's frontmatter still carries an `effort:` line.
   240	_sm_frontmatter_has_effort() {
   241	  awk 'NR == 1 && $0 != "---" { exit 1 } NR > 1 && $0 == "---" { exit 1 } NR > 1 && /^effort:/ { found = 1; exit 0 } END { exit (found ? 0 : 1) }' "$1"
   242	}
   243	
   244	_sm_cfg_set_false() {  # _sm_cfg_set_false <cfg> <yq-path>... ; verifies each
   245	  local cfg="$1"; shift
   246	  [[ -f "$cfg" ]] || : > "$cfg"
   247	  local p
   248	  for p in "$@"; do
   249	    P="$p" yq -i 'eval(strenv(P)) = false' "$cfg" 2>/dev/null || return 1
   250	    [[ "$(P="$p" yq -r 'eval(strenv(P))' "$cfg" 2>/dev/null)" == "false" ]] || return 1
   251	  done
   252	  return 0
   253	}
   254	
   255	apply_arm_toggles() {
   256	  local ws="$1" toggles="${2:-}" arm="${3:-}"
   257	  [[ -d "$ws" ]] || { _sm_err "apply_arm_toggles: workspace not found: $ws"; return 2; }
   258	  [[ -n "$toggles" ]] || toggles='{}'
   259	  jq -e 'type == "object"' >/dev/null 2>&1 <<<"$toggles" || { _sm_err "arm '$arm' toggles are not a JSON object"; return 2; }
   260	  local eval_dir="$ws/.eval"

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
     2	# =============================================================================
     3	# pipeline-run.sh — the cycle-130 ablation pipeline executor (SDD §1.4 D-4.1 … D-4.10, §5.6)
     4	#
     5	# Runs ONE task under ONE arm: materialises a sandbox repository (the task's
     6	# fixture tree, or the review-catch PR under pr/, plus the Loa mount from the
     7	# pinned --source-tree), then drives Loa's phases as separate `claude -p`
     8	# sessions inside it, records every phase, enforces the per-run cap and writes
     9	# meta/pipeline.json. One executor serves every task type (D-4.1):
    10	#   review-catch                      REVIEW → AUDIT
    11	#   bug-fix | refactor | feature-build PLAN → IMPLEMENT → REVIEW → FIX? → AUDIT → FIX?
    12	# A FIX runs only when the gate before it wrote a CHANGES_REQUIRED LOA-VERDICT
    13	# trailer (the last `<!-- LOA-VERDICT {…} -->` line of
    14	# grimoires/loa/a2a/sprint-1/engineer-feedback.md resp. auditor-sprint-feedback.md);
    15	# a FIX that does not run is recorded `skipped: true`.
    16	# Arms edit the phase set (D-4.2): `sprint_plan: false` drops PLAN; `gates: false`
    17	# ends after IMPLEMENT; `loa_mount: false` runs one BARE session (no mount);
    18	# `flatline: false` keeps PLAN with the Flatline step off; `context_resets: false`
    19	# runs PLAN, IMPLEMENT and FIX as ONE implementer session (`--resume <session_id>`
    20	# from the first session's system/init event) while REVIEW and AUDIT stay separate.
    21	# The suite's `phase_sets[<review-catch|build>]` and an arm's `phases` override the
    22	# default phase list; the toggle edits above apply on top.
    23	#
    24	# Usage:
    25	#   pipeline-run.sh --task-yaml F --arm ID --run-dir D --run-id R --trial N \
    26	#                   --source-tree DIR --suite-file F [--max-run-usd 12] \
    27	#                   [--executor container|host] [--image IMG] [--claude-bin B] \
    28	#                   [--docker-bin D] [--phase-models JSON] [--phase-timeouts JSON] [--dry-run]
    29	#
    30	# Options:
    31	#   --task-yaml F       task.yaml (SDD §3.2); its directory holds TASK.md
    32	#   --arm ID            arm id declared in the suite file (`arms[].id`)
    33	#   --run-dir D         run directory to create (must not exist or be empty);
    34	#                       alias --workspace
    35	#   --run-id R          run id recorded in pipeline.json
    36	#   --trial N           trial number
    37	#   --source-tree DIR   the pinned Loa tree the mount is copied from
    38	#   --suite-file F      evals/suites/ablation-2.0.yaml (read with yq -o=json)
    39	#   --max-run-usd USD   per-run cap (default 12; config evals.ablation.run_cap_usd)
    40	#   --executor MODE     container (default; DEC-0411) or host
    41	#   --image IMG         container image (default loa-ablation:258)
    42	#   --claude-bin B      host-mode CLI (default $EVAL_CLAUDE_BIN, else claude)
    43	#   --docker-bin D      docker CLI (default $EVAL_DOCKER_BIN, else docker)
    44	#   --phase-models JSON {"PLAN": "<model id>", …} override ($LOA_EVAL_PHASE_MODELS)
    45	#   --phase-timeouts JSON {"IMPLEMENT": <seconds>, …} override
    46	#   --dry-run           print the phase plan and exit 0; nothing is created
    47	#
    48	# Run directory layout (DEC-0413 — the grader never reads meta/):
    49	#   sandbox/     the agent's tree (its own .git initialised at `base`)
    50	#   snapshots/   <label>.bundle + index.json ({IMPLEMENT|FIX1|FIX2: commit}) after
    51	#                IMPLEMENT and each FIX
    52	#   transcripts/ events-<label>.jsonl (stream-json), stderr-<label>.log
    53	#   eval/        model-invoke.jsonl, cost-ledger.jsonl (copied out of
    54	#                sandbox/.eval/ after every phase), adversarial-*.json
    55	#   meta/        pipeline.json, phase-<label>.argv.json (argv + captured env),
    56	#                prompt-<label>.md, arm, arm-evidence.txt, arm-env, refused.json,
    57	#                home/ (container mode: the per-run HOME; deleted at exit)
    58	#
    59	# Session (D-4.3, DEC-0394 as amended, DEC-0412): `claude -p <prompt> --output-format
    60	# stream-json --verbose --model <id> --permission-mode bypassPermissions
    61	# --dangerously-skip-permissions --setting-sources project --tools <list>
    62	# --max-turns <cap> [--effort <v>] [--resume <id>]`, cwd sandbox/, with exactly this
    63	# environment: PATH HOME LANG LC_ALL TERM TMPDIR CLAUDE_CODE_USE_BEDROCK
    64	# CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL LOA_MODELINV_LOG_PATH LOA_COST_LEDGER_PATH
    65	# GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1 GH_CONFIG_DIR=<sandbox/.eval/gh-empty>,
    66	# the Bedrock route's pass-through keys when set in the driver's environment
    67	# (AWS_REGION AWS_DEFAULT_REGION AWS_PROFILE AWS_BEARER_TOKEN_BEDROCK
    68	# ANTHROPIC_BEDROCK_REGION_PREFIX ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_{OPUS,SONNET,HAIKU}_MODEL), and the
    69	# arm's LOA_* variables (LOA_ADVERSARIAL_REVIEW_ENFORCE=false for gates: false).
    70	# A python3 -I exec shim closes every descriptor above 2 and keeps exactly those keys;
    71	# values reach it through the environment, never argv, so AWS_BEARER_TOKEN_BEDROCK
    72	# appears in no argv, capture or log (phase-<label>.argv.json records it as "<set>").
    73	# `timeout --signal=TERM --kill-after=15` bounds the CLI.
    74	# Container mode (D-4.9, DEC-0411 as amended) runs the same command inside
    75	#   docker run --rm --name <n> --user <uid>:<gid> --network bridge --read-only
    76	#     --tmpfs /tmp:rw,size=1g --pids-limit 512 --memory 4g --cpus 2
    77	#     -v <run>/sandbox:/workspace:rw -v <run>/meta/home:/home/evaluser:rw
    78	#     -w /workspace -e <KEY=value…> -e AWS_BEARER_TOKEN_BEDROCK <image> python3 -I -c <shim> … claude …
    79	# Exactly two mounts. meta/home/ (mode 0700) holds copies of $HOME/.codex/{auth.json,
    80	# config.toml} when present and empty .claude/ and .aws/; the CLI's session store
    81	# lives there for the whole run, so A6's --resume works across phases. No ~/.claude
    82	# file is ever copied. The directory is deleted at exit and on interrupt.
    83	# image_digest = the image's RepoDigest or id (container), else the fingerprint (host).
    84	# Versions: `fingerprint` is computed from the HOST toolchain; in container mode the
    85	# toolchain that runs the phases is the image's (Claude Code 2.1.299, codex 0.137.0 by
    86	# Dockerfile.ablation), so image_digest identifies the batch's versions. On 2026-10-15
    87	# the host CLI was 2.1.300 while the image pins 2.1.299; every arm runs in the container.
    88	#
    89	# Cap and watchdog (D-4.6, D-4.10): while a phase runs the driver re-prices the
    90	# stream's assistant-turn usage every $LOA_EVAL_WATCHDOG_POLL_S seconds (default 1)
    91	# from per-token prices fetched once per model (pricing.py; $LOA_EVAL_PRICING_JSON
    92	# overrides) and SIGTERMs the phase when spent + estimate ≥ the cap (cap_turn
    93	# recorded). After each phase the result's total_cost_usd (authoritative) plus the
    94	# sandbox cost-ledger rows written during the phase are added; ≥ cap → cap_failure.
    95	#
    96	# Exit codes:
    97	#   0  finished (any verdict)                                   status completed
    98	#   1  agent error: a phase exited non-zero or timed out        status agent_error
    99	#   2  infrastructure: usage, refused arm/type, mount/toggle failure, CLI/docker

   101	#   3  cap failure (run stopped at the cap)                     status cap_failure

   104	# pipeline.json is written for every exit except usage errors and --dry-run; it is

   106	# record (ablation-row.sh reads `running` as interrupted).
   107	#
   108	# Env: EVAL_CLAUDE_BIN, EVAL_DOCKER_BIN, LOA_EVAL_PHASE_MODELS, LOA_EVAL_PRICING_JSON,

   111	#
   112	# Mount library: lib/sandbox-mount.sh beside this script, sourced by a literal path.

     3	# pipeline-run.sh — the cycle-130 ablation pipeline executor (SDD §1.4 D-4.1 … D-4.10, §5.6)
     4	#
     5	# Runs ONE task under ONE arm: materialises a sandbox repository (the task's
     6	# fixture tree, or the review-catch PR under pr/, plus the Loa mount from the
     7	# pinned --source-tree), then drives Loa's phases as separate `claude -p`

    13	# trailer (the last `<!-- LOA-VERDICT {…} -->` line of
    14	# grimoires/loa/a2a/sprint-1/engineer-feedback.md resp. auditor-sprint-feedback.md);
    15	# a FIX that does not run is recorded `skipped: true`.
    16	# Arms edit the phase set (D-4.2): `sprint_plan: false` drops PLAN; `gates: false`
    17	# ends after IMPLEMENT; `loa_mount: false` runs one BARE session (no mount);
    18	# `flatline: false` keeps PLAN with the Flatline step off; `context_resets: false`
    19	# runs PLAN, IMPLEMENT and FIX as ONE implementer session (`--resume <session_id>`
    20	# from the first session's system/init event) while REVIEW and AUDIT stay separate.
    21	# The suite's `phase_sets[<review-catch|build>]` and an arm's `phases` override the
    22	# default phase list; the toggle edits above apply on top.

   337	  printf '%s\n' "$ROW"
   338	fi

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
     2	# =============================================================================
     3	# took-effect.sh — prove an arm's configuration took effect, from run artefacts
     4	# (cycle-130 FR-3/FR-7, SDD §1.4 D-4.2, §5.10; DEC-0418)
     5	#
     6	# Evaluates the rule ids the suite file lists under the arm's `took_effect` against
     7	# one run directory written by pipeline-run.sh (or every run under --batch-dir).
     8	# Evidence is read from what the run produced — meta/pipeline.json, the
     9	# meta/phase-<label>.argv.json captures (argv + environment), eval/model-invoke.jsonl,
    10	# the dissent envelopes and the sandbox tree — never from what the agent said.
    11	#
    12	# Rules:
    13	#   no_dot_claude              sandbox has no .claude/ and no CLAUDE.md
    14	#   no_system_prompt           no argv carries --append-system-prompt-file
    15	#   no_audit_rows              no sandbox/.run/audit.jsonl (no hook ran)
    16	#   all_phases_present         the phase records equal the arm's phase set for the task
    17	#                              type (skipped FIX rounds count as records); a run that
    18	#                              stopped early (cap_failure, agent_error, interrupted)
    19	#                              passes when its records are a prefix of the set
    20	#   no_plan_phase              no PLAN record
    21	#   one_voice_planned          both envelopes (review, audit) say companion_voice.planned false
    22	#   no_gate_phases             no REVIEW, AUDIT or FIX record
    23	#   enforce_env_false          every captured phase env has LOA_ADVERSARIAL_REVIEW_ENFORCE=false
    24	#   no_flatline_rows           no eval/ MODELINV row whose calling_primitive starts with
    25	#                              flatline, and sandbox/grimoires/loa/sprint.md exists
    26	#   implementer_single_session one non-null session_id across the executed PLAN, IMPLEMENT
    27	#                              and FIX records, and every continuation's argv resumes it
    28	#   gates_separate_sessions    REVIEW and AUDIT session ids are non-null, distinct from
    29	#                              each other and from every implementer session id
    30	#   effort_flag_medium         every argv carries --effort medium
    31	#   skill_effort_stripped      no sandbox/.claude/skills/*/SKILL.md frontmatter has an ^effort:
    32	#                              line (the block between the first two `---` lines; body lines
    33	#                              are not frontmatter)
    34	#   integrity_clean            arm_evidence.manifest_sha256 is present and every entry of
    35	#                              sandbox/.claude/checksums.json hashes to its recorded value
    36	#                              (Python hashlib walk); a loa_mount: false arm passes with
    37	#                              "no mount"
    38	#   applicability_refused      a refusal record (meta/refused.json) names this arm and a task
    39	#                              type outside its task_types; a run that was not refused passes
    40	#                              when its task type is inside task_types (and fails otherwise)
    41	# A refusal record is evaluated on applicability_refused alone.
    42	#
    43	# Usage:
    44	#   took-effect.sh --run-dir D --suite-file F [--arm ID] [--json]
    45	#   took-effect.sh --batch-dir D --suite-file F [--arm ID] [--json]
    46	#
    47	# Output: `arm <id>: <rule> OK|FAIL <evidence>` per rule, then `arm <id>: OK` or
    48	# `arm <id>: FAIL (<n> of <m> rules)`; --batch-dir adds `took-effect: <runs> runs, <k> failed`.
    49	# --json prints one object per run ({run_dir, arm, ok, rules: [{rule, ok, evidence}]}).
    50	#
    51	# Exit codes:
    52	#   0  every rule OK
    53	#   1  any rule FAIL
    54	#   2  usage error (missing files, unknown arm)
    55	#
    56	# Tested by evals/tests/took-effect.bats (fixture runs under
    57	# evals/tests/fixtures/ablation-runs/).
    58	# =============================================================================
    59	set -euo pipefail
    60	export LC_ALL=C
    61	
    62	# Hashing is Python hashlib: no harness script sources .claude/ code (eval.yml
    63	# "Validate grader trust boundary").
    64	
    65	RUN_DIR="" BATCH_DIR="" SUITE_FILE="" ARM_OPT="" JSON=false
    66	usage() { echo "took-effect.sh: $*" >&2; exit 2; }
    67	while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
    68	  case "$1" in
    69	    --run-dir)    RUN_DIR="${2:-}"; shift 2 ;;
    70	    --batch-dir)  BATCH_DIR="${2:-}"; shift 2 ;;
    71	    --suite-file) SUITE_FILE="${2:-}"; shift 2 ;;
    72	    --arm)        ARM_OPT="${2:-}"; shift 2 ;;
    73	    --json)       JSON=true; shift ;;
    74	    -h|--help)    sed -n '2,56p' "$0"; exit 0 ;;
    75	    *) usage "unknown argument: $1" ;;
    76	  esac
    77	done
    78	[[ -n "$SUITE_FILE" && -f "$SUITE_FILE" ]] || usage "missing or unreadable --suite-file"
    79	[[ -n "$RUN_DIR" || -n "$BATCH_DIR" ]] || usage "one of --run-dir or --batch-dir is required"
    80	[[ -z "$RUN_DIR" || -z "$BATCH_DIR" ]] || usage "--run-dir and --batch-dir are exclusive"
    81	SUITE_JSON="$(yq -o=json '.' "$SUITE_FILE")" || usage "suite file does not parse"
    82	
    83	# ---- rule helpers: each sets EVID and returns 0 (OK) / 1 (FAIL) --------------------
    84	EVID=""
    85	argv_files() { local f; for f in "$R/meta"/phase-*.argv.json; do [[ -f "$f" ]] && printf '%s\n' "$f"; done; return 0; }
    86	envelope() {  # envelope <gate> → path or empty
    87	  local f="$R/sandbox/grimoires/loa/a2a/sprint-1/adversarial-$1.json"
    88	  [[ -f "$f" ]] || f="$R/eval/adversarial-$1.json"
    89	  [[ -f "$f" ]] && printf '%s' "$f"; return 0
    90	}
    91	
    92	expected_labels() {  # the arm's phase set for this run's task type (pipeline-run.sh's plan)
    93	  local type kind
    94	  type="$(jq -r '.task_type // ""' "$R/meta/pipeline.json")"
    95	  if [[ "$type" == review-catch ]]; then kind=review-catch; else kind=build; fi
    96	  jq -r -n --argjson arm "$ARM_DEF" --argjson suite "$SUITE_JSON" --arg kind "$kind" \
    97	    --argjson tg "$(jq -c '.arm_toggles // {}' "$R/meta/pipeline.json")" '
    98	    (if $kind == "review-catch" then ["REVIEW","AUDIT"] else ["PLAN","IMPLEMENT","REVIEW","FIX","AUDIT","FIX"] end) as $dflt
    99	    | ($arm.phases // $suite.phase_sets[$kind] // $dflt) as $p0
   100	    | (if ($tg.loa_mount == false) then ["BARE"] else $p0 end) as $p1
   101	    | (if ($tg.sprint_plan == false) then ($p1 | map(select(. != "PLAN"))) else $p1 end) as $p2
   102	    | (if ($tg.gates == false) and ($p2 | index("IMPLEMENT")) != null then $p2[0:(($p2 | index("IMPLEMENT")) + 1)] else $p2 end) as $p3
   103	    | reduce $p3[] as $n ({out: [], fix: 0};
   104	        if $n == "FIX" then .fix += 1 | .out += ["FIX" + (.fix | tostring)] else .out += [$n] end)
   105	    | .out | join(",")'
   106	}
   107	
   108	rule_no_dot_claude() {
   109	  if [[ -e "$R/sandbox/.claude" || -e "$R/sandbox/CLAUDE.md" ]]; then EVID="sandbox has .claude/ or CLAUDE.md"; return 1; fi
   110	  EVID="sandbox has no .claude/ and no CLAUDE.md"
   111	}
   112	rule_no_system_prompt() {
   113	  local f n=0 hit=""
   114	  while IFS= read -r f; do
   115	    n=$((n + 1))
   116	    jq -e '(.argv // []) | index("--append-system-prompt-file") != null' "$f" >/dev/null 2>&1 && hit="$hit $(basename "$f")"
   117	  done < <(argv_files)
   118	  [[ $n -gt 0 ]] || { EVID="no phase argv captured"; return 1; }
   119	  [[ -z "$hit" ]] || { EVID="--append-system-prompt-file in$hit"; return 1; }
   120	  EVID="no --append-system-prompt-file in $n argv"
   121	}
   122	rule_no_audit_rows() {
   123	  [[ -e "$R/sandbox/.run/audit.jsonl" ]] && { EVID="sandbox/.run/audit.jsonl exists"; return 1; }
   124	  EVID="no sandbox/.run/audit.jsonl"
   125	}
   126	rule_all_phases_present() {
   127	  local want got st
   128	  want="$(expected_labels)"
   129	  got="$(jq -r '[.phases // [] | .[] | .label] | join(",")' "$R/meta/pipeline.json")"
   130	  st="$(jq -r '.status // ""' "$R/meta/pipeline.json")"
   131	  if [[ "$got" == "$want" ]]; then EVID="phases $got"; return 0; fi
   132	  case "$st" in
   133	    cap_failure|agent_error|interrupted|running)
   134	      if [[ -n "$got" && ",$want," == ",$got,"* ]]; then EVID="phases $got (run stopped: $st; set $want)"; return 0; fi ;;
   135	  esac
   136	  EVID="phases ${got:-none}, want $want (status $st)"; return 1
   137	}
   138	rule_no_plan_phase() {
   139	  local n; n="$(jq '[.phases // [] | .[] | select(.name == "PLAN")] | length' "$R/meta/pipeline.json")"
   140	  [[ "$n" -eq 0 ]] || { EVID="$n PLAN record(s)"; return 1; }
   141	  EVID="no PLAN record"
   142	}
   143	rule_one_voice_planned() {
   144	  local g f v bad="" ev=""
   145	  for g in review audit; do
   146	    f="$(envelope "$g")"
   147	    if [[ -z "$f" ]]; then bad="$bad $g:missing"; continue; fi
   148	    v="$(jq -r 'if (.metadata.companion_voice | type) == "object" then .metadata.companion_voice.planned
   149	                elif (.companion_voice | type) == "object" then .companion_voice.planned else "absent" end | tostring' "$f" 2>/dev/null || echo unreadable)"
   150	    ev="$ev $g:planned=$v"
   151	    [[ "$v" == false ]] || bad="$bad $g:planned=$v"
   152	  done
   153	  [[ -z "$bad" ]] || { EVID="companion_voice${bad}"; return 1; }
   154	  EVID="companion_voice${ev}"
   155	}
   156	rule_no_gate_phases() {
   157	  local got; got="$(jq -r '[.phases // [] | .[] | select(.name == "REVIEW" or .name == "AUDIT" or .name == "FIX") | .label] | join(",")' "$R/meta/pipeline.json")"
   158	  [[ -z "$got" ]] || { EVID="gate records $got"; return 1; }
   159	  EVID="no REVIEW, AUDIT or FIX record"
   160	}
   161	rule_enforce_env_false() {
   162	  local f n=0 bad=""
   163	  while IFS= read -r f; do
   164	    n=$((n + 1))
   165	    [[ "$(jq -r '.env.LOA_ADVERSARIAL_REVIEW_ENFORCE // "unset"' "$f")" == false ]] || bad="$bad $(basename "$f" .argv.json)"
   166	  done < <(argv_files)
   167	  [[ $n -gt 0 ]] || { EVID="no phase argv captured"; return 1; }
   168	  [[ -z "$bad" ]] || { EVID="LOA_ADVERSARIAL_REVIEW_ENFORCE not false in$bad"; return 1; }
   169	  EVID="LOA_ADVERSARIAL_REVIEW_ENFORCE=false in $n/$n phase env"
   170	}
   171	rule_no_flatline_rows() {
   172	  local n=0
   173	  if [[ -f "$R/eval/model-invoke.jsonl" ]]; then
   174	    n="$(jq -R -n '[inputs | fromjson? | select(type == "object")
   175	           | (.payload.calling_primitive // .calling_primitive // .agent // "") | select(test("^flatline"))] | length' \
   176	         "$R/eval/model-invoke.jsonl")"
   177	  fi
   178	  [[ "$n" -eq 0 ]] || { EVID="$n flatline MODELINV row(s)"; return 1; }
   179	  [[ -f "$R/sandbox/grimoires/loa/sprint.md" ]] || { EVID="no flatline rows but no sandbox sprint.md"; return 1; }
   180	  EVID="no flatline MODELINV rows; sprint.md present"
   181	}
   182	rule_implementer_single_session() {
   183	  local ids n sid f bad=""
   184	  ids="$(jq -r '[.phases // [] | .[] | select(.skipped != true and (.name == "PLAN" or .name == "IMPLEMENT" or .name == "FIX")) | .session_id]' "$R/meta/pipeline.json")"
   185	  n="$(jq 'length' <<<"$ids")"
   186	  [[ "$n" -gt 0 ]] || { EVID="no implementer record"; return 1; }
   187	  [[ "$(jq '[.[] | select(. == null)] | length' <<<"$ids")" -eq 0 ]] || { EVID="an implementer record has no session_id"; return 1; }
   188	  [[ "$(jq 'unique | length' <<<"$ids")" -eq 1 ]] || { EVID="implementer session ids $(jq -r 'unique | join(",")' <<<"$ids")"; return 1; }
   189	  sid="$(jq -r '.[0]' <<<"$ids")"
   190	  while IFS= read -r f; do
   191	    case "$(jq -r '.name' "$f")" in PLAN|IMPLEMENT|FIX) ;; *) continue ;; esac
   192	    jq -e '.resume == null' "$f" >/dev/null && continue
   193	    jq -e --arg s "$sid" '.resume == $s and ((.argv | index("--resume")) as $i | $i != null and .argv[$i + 1] == $s)' "$f" >/dev/null \
   194	      || bad="$bad $(jq -r '.label' "$f")"
   195	  done < <(argv_files)
   196	  [[ -z "$bad" ]] || { EVID="continuation argv does not resume $sid:$bad"; return 1; }
   197	  EVID="one session $sid across $n implementer record(s)"
   198	}
   199	rule_gates_separate_sessions() {
   200	  local r a impl
   201	  r="$(jq -r '[.phases // [] | .[] | select(.name == "REVIEW" and .skipped != true) | .session_id][0] // "null"' "$R/meta/pipeline.json")"
   202	  a="$(jq -r '[.phases // [] | .[] | select(.name == "AUDIT" and .skipped != true) | .session_id][0] // "null"' "$R/meta/pipeline.json")"
   203	  impl="$(jq -c '[.phases // [] | .[] | select(.name == "PLAN" or .name == "IMPLEMENT" or .name == "FIX") | .session_id | select(. != null)] | unique' "$R/meta/pipeline.json")"
   204	  [[ "$r" != null && "$a" != null ]] || { EVID="gate session ids review=$r audit=$a"; return 1; }
   205	  [[ "$r" != "$a" ]] || { EVID="REVIEW and AUDIT share session $r"; return 1; }
   206	  if jq -e --arg r "$r" --arg a "$a" 'index($r) != null or index($a) != null' <<<"$impl" >/dev/null; then
   207	    EVID="a gate shares an implementer session"; return 1
   208	  fi
   209	  EVID="review $r, audit $a, implementer $(jq -r 'join(",")' <<<"$impl")"
   210	}
   211	rule_effort_flag_medium() {
   212	  local f n=0 ok=0
   213	  while IFS= read -r f; do
   214	    n=$((n + 1))
   215	    jq -e '(.argv // []) | (index("--effort")) as $i | $i != null and .[$i + 1] == "medium"' "$f" >/dev/null && ok=$((ok + 1))
   216	  done < <(argv_files)
   217	  [[ $n -gt 0 && $ok -eq $n ]] || { EVID="--effort medium on $ok/$n phases"; return 1; }
   218	  EVID="--effort medium on $ok/$n phases"
   219	}
   220	rule_skill_effort_stripped() {
   221	  local f n=0 hit=0
   222	  for f in "$R"/sandbox/.claude/skills/*/SKILL.md; do
   223	    [[ -f "$f" ]] || continue
   224	    n=$((n + 1))
   225	    # the YAML frontmatter only (first line `---` to the next `---`); a body line may say effort:
   226	    awk 'NR == 1 && $0 != "---" {exit} NR > 1 && $0 == "---" {exit} NR > 1 && /^effort:/ {hit = 1; exit} END {exit !hit}' "$f" \
   227	      && hit=$((hit + 1))
   228	  done
   229	  [[ $n -gt 0 ]] || { EVID="no sandbox SKILL.md"; return 1; }
   230	  [[ $hit -eq 0 ]] || { EVID="$hit/$n SKILL.md still carry effort:"; return 1; }
   231	  EVID="skill effort lines stripped $n/$n"
   232	}
   233	rule_integrity_clean() {
   234	  local man="$R/sandbox/.claude/checksums.json" msha out
   235	  if [[ "$(jq -r '.arm_toggles.loa_mount' "$R/meta/pipeline.json")" == false ]]; then
   236	    [[ -e "$R/sandbox/.claude" ]] && { EVID="loa_mount: false but sandbox has .claude/"; return 1; }
   237	    EVID="no mount (loa_mount: false)"; return 0
   238	  fi
   239	  msha="$(jq -r '.arm_evidence.manifest_sha256 // empty' "$R/meta/pipeline.json")"
   240	  [[ -n "$msha" && "$msha" != none ]] || { EVID="no arm_evidence.manifest_sha256"; return 1; }
   241	  [[ -f "$man" ]] && jq -e '.files | type == "object"' "$man" >/dev/null 2>&1 || { EVID="no sandbox .claude/checksums.json files map"; return 1; }
   242	  # one hashlib walk over every manifest entry: "<n> <tampered> <missing> <file-sha> <first problem>"
   243	  out="$(python3 -I -c '
   244	import hashlib, json, os, sys
   245	root, man = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2]
   246	def sha(p):
   247	    h = hashlib.sha256()
   248	    with open(p, "rb") as f:
   249	        for b in iter(lambda: f.read(1 << 20), b""):
   250	            h.update(b)
   251	    return h.hexdigest()
   252	files = json.load(open(man)).get("files") or {}
   253	bad = missing = 0; first = "-"
   254	for rel, want in sorted(files.items()):
   255	    p = os.path.join(root, rel)
   256	    if not os.path.isfile(p):
   257	        missing += 1; first = first if first != "-" else "missing " + rel
   258	    elif sha(p) != want:
   259	        bad += 1; first = first if first != "-" else "tampered " + rel
   260	print(len(files), bad, missing, sha(man), first)' "$R/sandbox" "$man")" || { EVID="hash walk failed"; return 1; }
   261	  local n bad missing filesha first
   262	  read -r n bad missing filesha first <<<"$out"
   263	  [[ "$n" -gt 0 ]] || { EVID="manifest lists no files"; return 1; }
   264	  if [[ "$bad" -gt 0 || "$missing" -gt 0 ]]; then EVID="$bad tampered, $missing missing of $n ($first)"; return 1; fi
   265	  EVID="$n manifest entries verified; manifest_sha256 ${msha:0:12}"
   266	  [[ "$filesha" == "$msha" ]] && EVID="$EVID (matches checksums.json)"
   267	  return 0
   268	}
   269	rule_applicability_refused() {
   270	  local f="$R/meta/refused.json" a t
   271	  if [[ ! -f "$f" ]]; then
   272	    # a run that was not refused: its task type must be one the arm declares
   273	    t="$(jq -r '.task_type // ""' "$R/meta/pipeline.json")"
   274	    local k=build; [[ "$t" == review-catch ]] && k=review-catch
   275	    if jq -e --arg k "$k" --arg t "$t" '(.task_types // ["all"]) as $tt | ($tt | index("all")) or ($tt | index($k)) or ($tt | index($t))' \
   276	         <<<"$ARM_DEF" >/dev/null; then
   277	      EVID="applicable: $t in task_types $(jq -c '.task_types // null' <<<"$ARM_DEF") (no refusal needed)"; return 0
   278	    fi
   279	    EVID="ran on $t outside task_types $(jq -c '.task_types // null' <<<"$ARM_DEF") without a refusal record"; return 1
   280	  fi
   281	  a="$(jq -r '.arm // ""' "$f")"; t="$(jq -r '.type // ""' "$f")"
   282	  [[ "$a" == "$ARM" && -n "$t" ]] || { EVID="refusal record names arm '$a' type '$t'"; return 1; }
   283	  local kind=build; [[ "$t" == review-catch ]] && kind=review-catch
   284	  if jq -e --arg k "$kind" --arg t "$t" '(.task_types // ["all"]) as $tt | ($tt | index("all")) or ($tt | index($k)) or ($tt | index($t))' \
   285	       <<<"$ARM_DEF" >/dev/null; then
   286	    EVID="arm task_types $(jq -c '.task_types' <<<"$ARM_DEF") include $t, yet the run was refused"; return 1
   287	  fi
   288	  EVID="refused $t (task_types $(jq -c '.task_types // null' <<<"$ARM_DEF"))"
   289	}
   290	
   291	# ---- one run ------------------------------------------------------------------------
   292	check_run() {  # check_run <run-dir> → prints lines; returns 0/1; 2 on usage problems
   293	  R="$1"
   294	  local arm rules rule fails=0 total=0 results='[]' ok
   295	  if [[ -n "$ARM_OPT" ]]; then arm="$ARM_OPT"
   296	  elif [[ -f "$R/meta/arm" ]]; then arm="$(sed -n '1p' "$R/meta/arm" | tr -d '[:space:]')"
   297	  elif [[ -f "$R/meta/refused.json" ]]; then arm="$(jq -r '.arm // ""' "$R/meta/refused.json")"
   298	  else arm="$(jq -r '.arm // ""' "$R/meta/pipeline.json" 2>/dev/null || true)"; fi
   299	  [[ -n "$arm" ]] || { echo "took-effect.sh: no arm for $R" >&2; return 2; }
   300	  ARM="$arm"
   301	  ARM_DEF="$(jq -c --arg a "$arm" '[.arms // [] | .[] | select(.id == $a)][0] // empty' <<<"$SUITE_JSON")"
   302	  [[ -n "$ARM_DEF" ]] || { echo "took-effect.sh: arm $arm is not declared in the suite" >&2; return 2; }
   303	  if [[ "$(jq -r '.absent // false' <<<"$ARM_DEF")" == true ]]; then
   304	    if [[ "$JSON" == true ]]; then jq -nc --arg d "$R" --arg arm "$arm" '{run_dir: $d, arm: $arm, ok: true, absent: true, rules: []}'
   305	    else printf 'arm %s: absent (component-absent; no rules)\n' "$arm"; fi
   306	    return 0
   307	  fi
   308	  if [[ -f "$R/meta/refused.json" ]]; then
   309	    rules="applicability_refused"
   310	  else
   311	    [[ -f "$R/meta/pipeline.json" ]] || { echo "took-effect.sh: no meta/pipeline.json under $R" >&2; return 2; }
   312	    rules="$(jq -r '(.took_effect // []) | .[]' <<<"$ARM_DEF")"
   313	    [[ -n "$rules" ]] || { echo "took-effect.sh: arm $arm lists no took_effect rules" >&2; return 2; }
   314	  fi
   315	  while IFS= read -r rule; do
   316	    [[ -n "$rule" ]] || continue
   317	    total=$((total + 1)); EVID=""
   318	    if declare -F "rule_$rule" >/dev/null; then
   319	      if "rule_$rule"; then ok=true; else ok=false; fi
   320	    else
   321	      ok=false; EVID="unknown rule id"
   322	    fi
   323	    [[ "$ok" == true ]] || fails=$((fails + 1))
   324	    if [[ "$JSON" == true ]]; then
   325	      results="$(jq -c --arg r "$rule" --argjson ok "$ok" --arg e "$EVID" '. + [{rule: $r, ok: $ok, evidence: $e}]' <<<"$results")"
   326	    else
   327	      printf 'arm %s: %s %s %s\n' "$arm" "$rule" "$([[ "$ok" == true ]] && echo OK || echo FAIL)" "$EVID"
   328	    fi
   329	  done <<<"$rules"
   330	  if [[ "$JSON" == true ]]; then
   331	    jq -nc --arg d "$R" --arg arm "$arm" --argjson rules "$results" --argjson ok "$([[ $fails -eq 0 ]] && echo true || echo false)" \
   332	      '{run_dir: $d, arm: $arm, ok: $ok, rules: $rules}'
   333	  elif [[ $fails -eq 0 ]]; then
   334	    printf 'arm %s: OK\n' "$arm"
   335	  else
   336	    printf 'arm %s: FAIL (%d of %d rules)\n' "$arm" "$fails" "$total"
   337	  fi
   338	  [[ $fails -eq 0 ]]
   339	}
   340

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
     2	# =============================================================================
     3	# took-effect.sh — prove an arm's configuration took effect, from run artefacts
     4	# (cycle-130 FR-3/FR-7, SDD §1.4 D-4.2, §5.10; DEC-0418)
     5	#
     6	# Evaluates the rule ids the suite file lists under the arm's `took_effect` against
     7	# one run directory written by pipeline-run.sh (or every run under --batch-dir).
     8	# Evidence is read from what the run produced — meta/pipeline.json, the
     9	# meta/phase-<label>.argv.json captures (argv + environment), eval/model-invoke.jsonl,
    10	# the dissent envelopes and the sandbox tree — never from what the agent said.
    11	#
    12	# Rules:
    13	#   no_dot_claude              sandbox has no .claude/ and no CLAUDE.md
    14	#   no_system_prompt           no argv carries --append-system-prompt-file
    15	#   no_audit_rows              no sandbox/.run/audit.jsonl (no hook ran)
    16	#   all_phases_present         the phase records equal the arm's phase set for the task
    17	#                              type (skipped FIX rounds count as records); a run that
    18	#                              stopped early (cap_failure, agent_error, interrupted)
    19	#                              passes when its records are a prefix of the set
    20	#   no_plan_phase              no PLAN record
    21	#   one_voice_planned          both envelopes (review, audit) say companion_voice.planned false
    22	#   no_gate_phases             no REVIEW, AUDIT or FIX record
    23	#   enforce_env_false          every captured phase env has LOA_ADVERSARIAL_REVIEW_ENFORCE=false
    24	#   no_flatline_rows           no eval/ MODELINV row whose calling_primitive starts with
    25	#                              flatline, and sandbox/grimoires/loa/sprint.md exists
    26	#   implementer_single_session one non-null session_id across the executed PLAN, IMPLEMENT
    27	#                              and FIX records, and every continuation's argv resumes it
    28	#   gates_separate_sessions    REVIEW and AUDIT session ids are non-null, distinct from
    29	#                              each other and from every implementer session id
    30	#   effort_flag_medium         every argv carries --effort medium
    31	#   skill_effort_stripped      no sandbox/.claude/skills/*/SKILL.md frontmatter has an ^effort:
    32	#                              line (the block between the first two `---` lines; body lines
    33	#                              are not frontmatter)
    34	#   integrity_clean            arm_evidence.manifest_sha256 is present and every entry of
    35	#                              sandbox/.claude/checksums.json hashes to its recorded value
    36	#                              (Python hashlib walk); a loa_mount: false arm passes with
    37	#                              "no mount"
    38	#   applicability_refused      a refusal record (meta/refused.json) names this arm and a task
    39	#                              type outside its task_types; a run that was not refused passes
    40	#                              when its task type is inside task_types (and fails otherwise)
    41	# A refusal record is evaluated on applicability_refused alone.
    42	#
    43	# Usage:
    44	#   took-effect.sh --run-dir D --suite-file F [--arm ID] [--json]
    45	#   took-effect.sh --batch-dir D --suite-file F [--arm ID] [--json]
    46	#
    47	# Output: `arm <id>: <rule> OK|FAIL <evidence>` per rule, then `arm <id>: OK` or
    48	# `arm <id>: FAIL (<n> of <m> rules)`; --batch-dir adds `took-effect: <runs> runs, <k> failed`.
    49	# --json prints one object per run ({run_dir, arm, ok, rules: [{rule, ok, evidence}]}).
    50	#
    51	# Exit codes:
    52	#   0  every rule OK
    53	#   1  any rule FAIL
    54	#   2  usage error (missing files, unknown arm)
    55	#
    56	# Tested by evals/tests/took-effect.bats (fixture runs under
    57	# evals/tests/fixtures/ablation-runs/).
    58	# =============================================================================
    59	set -euo pipefail
    60	export LC_ALL=C
    61	
    62	# Hashing is Python hashlib: no harness script sources .claude/ code (eval.yml
    63	# "Validate grader trust boundary").
    64	
    65	RUN_DIR="" BATCH_DIR="" SUITE_FILE="" ARM_OPT="" JSON=false
    66	usage() { echo "took-effect.sh: $*" >&2; exit 2; }
    67	while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
    68	  case "$1" in
    69	    --run-dir)    RUN_DIR="${2:-}"; shift 2 ;;
    70	    --batch-dir)  BATCH_DIR="${2:-}"; shift 2 ;;
    71	    --suite-file) SUITE_FILE="${2:-}"; shift 2 ;;
    72	    --arm)        ARM_OPT="${2:-}"; shift 2 ;;
    73	    --json)       JSON=true; shift ;;
    74	    -h|--help)    sed -n '2,56p' "$0"; exit 0 ;;
    75	    *) usage "unknown argument: $1" ;;
    76	  esac
    77	done
    78	[[ -n "$SUITE_FILE" && -f "$SUITE_FILE" ]] || usage "missing or unreadable --suite-file"
    79	[[ -n "$RUN_DIR" || -n "$BATCH_DIR" ]] || usage "one of --run-dir or --batch-dir is required"
    80	[[ -z "$RUN_DIR" || -z "$BATCH_DIR" ]] || usage "--run-dir and --batch-dir are exclusive"
    81	SUITE_JSON="$(yq -o=json '.' "$SUITE_FILE")" || usage "suite file does not parse"
    82	
    83	# ---- rule helpers: each sets EVID and returns 0 (OK) / 1 (FAIL) --------------------
    84	EVID=""
    85	argv_files() { local f; for f in "$R/meta"/phase-*.argv.json; do [[ -f "$f" ]] && printf '%s\n' "$f"; done; return 0; }
    86	envelope() {  # envelope <gate> → path or empty
    87	  local f="$R/sandbox/grimoires/loa/a2a/sprint-1/adversarial-$1.json"
    88	  [[ -f "$f" ]] || f="$R/eval/adversarial-$1.json"
    89	  [[ -f "$f" ]] && printf '%s' "$f"; return 0
    90	}
    91	
    92	expected_labels() {  # the arm's phase set for this run's task type (pipeline-run.sh's plan)
    93	  local type kind
    94	  type="$(jq -r '.task_type // ""' "$R/meta/pipeline.json")"
    95	  if [[ "$type" == review-catch ]]; then kind=review-catch; else kind=build; fi
    96	  jq -r -n --argjson arm "$ARM_DEF" --argjson suite "$SUITE_JSON" --arg kind "$kind" \
    97	    --argjson tg "$(jq -c '.arm_toggles // {}' "$R/meta/pipeline.json")" '
    98	    (if $kind == "review-catch" then ["REVIEW","AUDIT"] else ["PLAN","IMPLEMENT","REVIEW","FIX","AUDIT","FIX"] end) as $dflt
    99	    | ($arm.phases // $suite.phase_sets[$kind] // $dflt) as $p0
   100	    | (if ($tg.loa_mount == false) then ["BARE"] else $p0 end) as $p1
   101	    | (if ($tg.sprint_plan == false) then ($p1 | map(select(. != "PLAN"))) else $p1 end) as $p2
   102	    | (if ($tg.gates == false) and ($p2 | index("IMPLEMENT")) != null then $p2[0:(($p2 | index("IMPLEMENT")) + 1)] else $p2 end) as $p3
   103	    | reduce $p3[] as $n ({out: [], fix: 0};
   104	        if $n == "FIX" then .fix += 1 | .out += ["FIX" + (.fix | tostring)] else .out += [$n] end)
   105	    | .out | join(",")'
   106	}
   107	
   108	rule_no_dot_claude() {
   109	  if [[ -e "$R/sandbox/.claude" || -e "$R/sandbox/CLAUDE.md" ]]; then EVID="sandbox has .claude/ or CLAUDE.md"; return 1; fi
   110	  EVID="sandbox has no .claude/ and no CLAUDE.md"
   111	}
   112	rule_no_system_prompt() {
   113	  local f n=0 hit=""
   114	  while IFS= read -r f; do
   115	    n=$((n + 1))
   116	    jq -e '(.argv // []) | index("--append-system-prompt-file") != null' "$f" >/dev/null 2>&1 && hit="$hit $(basename "$f")"
   117	  done < <(argv_files)
   118	  [[ $n -gt 0 ]] || { EVID="no phase argv captured"; return 1; }
   119	  [[ -z "$hit" ]] || { EVID="--append-system-prompt-file in$hit"; return 1; }
   120	  EVID="no --append-system-prompt-file in $n argv"
   121	}
   122	rule_no_audit_rows() {
   123	  [[ -e "$R/sandbox/.run/audit.jsonl" ]] && { EVID="sandbox/.run/audit.jsonl exists"; return 1; }
   124	  EVID="no sandbox/.run/audit.jsonl"
   125	}
   126	rule_all_phases_present() {
   127	  local want got st
   128	  want="$(expected_labels)"
   129	  got="$(jq -r '[.phases // [] | .[] | .label] | join(",")' "$R/meta/pipeline.json")"
   130	  st="$(jq -r '.status // ""' "$R/meta/pipeline.json")"

   132	  case "$st" in
   133	    cap_failure|agent_error|interrupted|running)
   134	      if [[ -n "$got" && ",$want," == ",$got,"* ]]; then EVID="phases $got (run stopped: $st; set $want)"; return 0; fi ;;
   135	  esac
   136	  EVID="phases ${got:-none}, want $want (status $st)"; return 1
   137	}
   138	rule_no_plan_phase() {
   139	  local n; n="$(jq '[.phases // [] | .[] | select(.name == "PLAN")] | length' "$R/meta/pipeline.json")"
   140	  [[ "$n" -eq 0 ]] || { EVID="$n PLAN record(s)"; return 1; }
   141	  EVID="no PLAN record"

   143	rule_one_voice_planned() {
   144	  local g f v bad="" ev=""
   145	  for g in review audit; do
   146	    f="$(envelope "$g")"
   147	    if [[ -z "$f" ]]; then bad="$bad $g:missing"; continue; fi

   149	                elif (.companion_voice | type) == "object" then .companion_voice.planned else "absent" end | tostring' "$f" 2>/dev/null || echo unreadable)"

   156	rule_no_gate_phases() {
   157	  local got; got="$(jq -r '[.phases // [] | .[] | select(.name == "REVIEW" or .name == "AUDIT" or .name == "FIX") | .label] | join(",")' "$R/meta/pipeline.json")"
   158	  [[ -z "$got" ]] || { EVID="gate records $got"; return 1; }
   159	  EVID="no REVIEW, AUDIT or FIX record"

   161	rule_enforce_env_false() {
   162	  local f n=0 bad=""
   163	  while IFS= read -r f; do
   164	    n=$((n + 1))

   166	  done < <(argv_files)

   168	  [[ -z "$bad" ]] || { EVID="LOA_ADVERSARIAL_REVIEW_ENFORCE not false in$bad"; return 1; }
