   171	rule_no_flatline_rows() {
   172	  local n=0
   173	  if [[ -f "$R/eval/model-invoke.jsonl" ]]; then
   174	    n="$(jq -R -n '[inputs | fromjson? | select(type == "object")
   175	           | (.payload.calling_primitive // .calling_primitive // .agent // "") | select(test("^flatline"))] | length' \

   179	  [[ -f "$R/sandbox/grimoires/loa/sprint.md" ]] || { EVID="no flatline rows but no sandbox sprint.md"; return 1; }

   182	rule_implementer_single_session() {
   183	  local ids n sid f bad=""
   184	  ids="$(jq -r '[.phases // [] | .[] | select(.skipped != true and (.name == "PLAN" or .name == "IMPLEMENT" or .name == "FIX")) | .session_id]' "$R/meta/pipeline.json")"
   185	  n="$(jq 'length' <<<"$ids")"
   186	  [[ "$n" -gt 0 ]] || { EVID="no implementer record"; return 1; }
   187	  [[ "$(jq '[.[] | select(. == null)] | length' <<<"$ids")" -eq 0 ]] || { EVID="an implementer record has no session_id"; return 1; }
   188	  [[ "$(jq 'unique | length' <<<"$ids")" -eq 1 ]] || { EVID="implementer session ids $(jq -r 'unique | join(",")' <<<"$ids")"; return 1; }
   189	  sid="$(jq -r '.[0]' <<<"$ids")"
   190	  while IFS= read -r f; do
   191	    case "$(jq -r '.name' "$f")" in PLAN|IMPLEMENT|FIX) ;; *) continue ;; esac
   192	    jq -e '.resume == null' "$f" >/dev/null && continue
   193	    jq -e --arg s "$sid" '.resume == $s and ((.argv | index("--resume")) as $i | $i != null and .argv[$i + 1] == $s)' "$f" >/dev/null \
   194	      || bad="$bad $(jq -r '.label' "$f")"
   195	  done < <(argv_files)
   196	  [[ -z "$bad" ]] || { EVID="continuation argv does not resume $sid:$bad"; return 1; }
   197	  EVID="one session $sid across $n implementer record(s)"
   198	}
   199	rule_gates_separate_sessions() {
   200	  local r a impl
   201	  r="$(jq -r '[.phases // [] | .[] | select(.name == "REVIEW" and .skipped != true) | .session_id][0] // "null"' "$R/meta/pipeline.json")"
   202	  a="$(jq -r '[.phases // [] | .[] | select(.name == "AUDIT" and .skipped != true) | .session_id][0] // "null"' "$R/meta/pipeline.json")"

   204	  [[ "$r" != null && "$a" != null ]] || { EVID="gate session ids review=$r audit=$a"; return 1; }
   205	  [[ "$r" != "$a" ]] || { EVID="REVIEW and AUDIT share session $r"; return 1; }
   206	  if jq -e --arg r "$r" --arg a "$a" 'index($r) != null or index($a) != null' <<<"$impl" >/dev/null; then

   208	  fi
   209	  EVID="review $r, audit $a, implementer $(jq -r 'join(",")' <<<"$impl")"

   211	rule_effort_flag_medium() {
   212	  local f n=0 ok=0
   213	  while IFS= read -r f; do
   214	    n=$((n + 1))
   215	    jq -e '(.argv // []) | (index("--effort")) as $i | $i != null and .[$i + 1] == "medium"' "$f" >/dev/null && ok=$((ok + 1))
   216	  done < <(argv_files)
   217	  [[ $n -gt 0 && $ok -eq $n ]] || { EVID="--effort medium on $ok/$n phases"; return 1; }
   218	  EVID="--effort medium on $ok/$n phases"
   219	}
   220	rule_skill_effort_stripped() {
   221	  local f n=0 hit=0
   222	  for f in "$R"/sandbox/.claude/skills/*/SKILL.md; do
   223	    [[ -f "$f" ]] || continue
   224	    n=$((n + 1))
   225	    # the YAML frontmatter only (first line `---` to the next `---`); a body line may say effort:
   226	    awk 'NR == 1 && $0 != "---" {exit} NR > 1 && $0 == "---" {exit} NR > 1 && /^effort:/ {hit = 1; exit} END {exit !hit}' "$f" \
   227	      && hit=$((hit + 1))
   228	  done
   229	  [[ $n -gt 0 ]] || { EVID="no sandbox SKILL.md"; return 1; }
   230	  [[ $hit -eq 0 ]] || { EVID="$hit/$n SKILL.md still carry effort:"; return 1; }
   231	  EVID="skill effort lines stripped $n/$n"
   232	}
   233	rule_integrity_clean() {
   234	  local man="$R/sandbox/.claude/checksums.json" msha out
   235	  if [[ "$(jq -r '.arm_toggles.loa_mount' "$R/meta/pipeline.json")" == false ]]; then
   236	    [[ -e "$R/sandbox/.claude" ]] && { EVID="loa_mount: false but sandbox has .claude/"; return 1; }
   237	    EVID="no mount (loa_mount: false)"; return 0
   238	  fi
   239	  msha="$(jq -r '.arm_evidence.manifest_sha256 // empty' "$R/meta/pipeline.json")"
   240	  [[ -n "$msha" && "$msha" != none ]] || { EVID="no arm_evidence.manifest_sha256"; return 1; }
   241	  [[ -f "$man" ]] && jq -e '.files | type == "object"' "$man" >/dev/null 2>&1 || { EVID="no sandbox .claude/checksums.json files map"; return 1; }
   242	  # one hashlib walk over every manifest entry: "<n> <tampered> <missing> <file-sha> <first problem>"
   243	  out="$(python3 -I -c '
   244	import hashlib, json, os, sys
   245	root, man = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2]
   246	def sha(p):
   247	    h = hashlib.sha256()
   248	    with open(p, "rb") as f:
   249	        for b in iter(lambda: f.read(1 << 20), b""):
   250	            h.update(b)
   251	    return h.hexdigest()
   252	files = json.load(open(man)).get("files") or {}
   253	bad = missing = 0; first = "-"
   254	for rel, want in sorted(files.items()):
   255	    p = os.path.join(root, rel)
   256	    if not os.path.isfile(p):
   257	        missing += 1; first = first if first != "-" else "missing " + rel
   258	    elif sha(p) != want:
   259	        bad += 1; first = first if first != "-" else "tampered " + rel
   260	print(len(files), bad, missing, sha(man), first)' "$R/sandbox" "$man")" || { EVID="hash walk failed"; return 1; }
   261	  local n bad missing filesha first
   262	  read -r n bad missing filesha first <<<"$out"
   263	  [[ "$n" -gt 0 ]] || { EVID="manifest lists no files"; return 1; }
   264	  if [[ "$bad" -gt 0 || "$missing" -gt 0 ]]; then EVID="$bad tampered, $missing missing of $n ($first)"; return 1; fi
   265	  EVID="$n manifest entries verified; manifest_sha256 ${msha:0:12}"
   266	  [[ "$filesha" == "$msha" ]] && EVID="$EVID (matches checksums.json)"
   267	  return 0
   268	}
   269	rule_applicability_refused() {
   270	  local f="$R/meta/refused.json" a t
   271	  if [[ ! -f "$f" ]]; then
   272	    # a run that was not refused: its task type must be one the arm declares
   273	    t="$(jq -r '.task_type // ""' "$R/meta/pipeline.json")"
   274	    local k=build; [[ "$t" == review-catch ]] && k=review-catch
   275	    if jq -e --arg k "$k" --arg t "$t" '(.task_types // ["all"]) as $tt | ($tt | index("all")) or ($tt | index($k)) or ($tt | index($t))' \
   276	         <<<"$ARM_DEF" >/dev/null; then
   277	      EVID="applicable: $t in task_types $(jq -c '.task_types // null' <<<"$ARM_DEF") (no refusal needed)"; return 0
   278	    fi
   279	    EVID="ran on $t outside task_types $(jq -c '.task_types // null' <<<"$ARM_DEF") without a refusal record"; return 1
   280	  fi
   281	  a="$(jq -r '.arm // ""' "$f")"; t="$(jq -r '.type // ""' "$f")"
   282	  [[ "$a" == "$ARM" && -n "$t" ]] || { EVID="refusal record names arm '$a' type '$t'"; return 1; }
   283	  local kind=build; [[ "$t" == review-catch ]] && kind=review-catch
   284	  if jq -e --arg k "$kind" --arg t "$t" '(.task_types // ["all"]) as $tt | ($tt | index("all")) or ($tt | index($k)) or ($tt | index($t))' \
   285	       <<<"$ARM_DEF" >/dev/null; then
   286	    EVID="arm task_types $(jq -c '.task_types' <<<"$ARM_DEF") include $t, yet the run was refused"; return 1
   287	  fi
   288	  EVID="refused $t (task_types $(jq -c '.task_types // null' <<<"$ARM_DEF"))"
   289	}
   290	
   291	# ---- one run ------------------------------------------------------------------------
   292	check_run() {  # check_run <run-dir> → prints lines; returns 0/1; 2 on usage problems
   293	  R="$1"
   294	  local arm rules rule fails=0 total=0 results='[]' ok
   295	  if [[ -n "$ARM_OPT" ]]; then arm="$ARM_OPT"
   296	  elif [[ -f "$R/meta/arm" ]]; then arm="$(sed -n '1p' "$R/meta/arm" | tr -d '[:space:]')"
   297	  elif [[ -f "$R/meta/refused.json" ]]; then arm="$(jq -r '.arm // ""' "$R/meta/refused.json")"
   298	  else arm="$(jq -r '.arm // ""' "$R/meta/pipeline.json" 2>/dev/null || true)"; fi
   299	  [[ -n "$arm" ]] || { echo "took-effect.sh: no arm for $R" >&2; return 2; }
   300	  ARM="$arm"
   301	  ARM_DEF="$(jq -c --arg a "$arm" '[.arms // [] | .[] | select(.id == $a)][0] // empty' <<<"$SUITE_JSON")"
   302	  [[ -n "$ARM_DEF" ]] || { echo "took-effect.sh: arm $arm is not declared in the suite" >&2; return 2; }
   303	  if [[ "$(jq -r '.absent // false' <<<"$ARM_DEF")" == true ]]; then
   304	    if [[ "$JSON" == true ]]; then jq -nc --arg d "$R" --arg arm "$arm" '{run_dir: $d, arm: $arm, ok: true, absent: true, rules: []}'
   305	    else printf 'arm %s: absent (component-absent; no rules)\n' "$arm"; fi
   306	    return 0
   307	  fi
   308	  if [[ -f "$R/meta/refused.json" ]]; then
   309	    rules="applicability_refused"
   310	  else
   311	    [[ -f "$R/meta/pipeline.json" ]] || { echo "took-effect.sh: no meta/pipeline.json under $R" >&2; return 2; }
   312	    rules="$(jq -r '(.took_effect // []) | .[]' <<<"$ARM_DEF")"
   313	    [[ -n "$rules" ]] || { echo "took-effect.sh: arm $arm lists no took_effect rules" >&2; return 2; }
   314	  fi
   315	  while IFS= read -r rule; do
   316	    [[ -n "$rule" ]] || continue
   317	    total=$((total + 1)); EVID=""
   318	    if declare -F "rule_$rule" >/dev/null; then
   319	      if "rule_$rule"; then ok=true; else ok=false; fi
   320	    else
   321	      ok=false; EVID="unknown rule id"
   322	    fi
   323	    [[ "$ok" == true ]] || fails=$((fails + 1))

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
     2	# =============================================================================
     3	# spend.sh — cycle-130 cycle spend (SDD §5.11, PRD FR-2, DEC-0363)
     4	#
     5	# Prints what the cycle has spent: the run rows' cost_usd plus the operator
     6	# cost ledger's cost_micro_usd since the kickoff timestamp, against the cap.
     7	#
     8	# Usage:
     9	#   spend.sh [--since TS] [--runs FILE…] [--ledger FILE] [--cap USD]
    10	#            [--reserve USD] [--json]
    11	#
    12	#   --since TS     ledger rows with ts >= TS count (default 2026-10-14T13:50:00Z,
    13	#                  the cycle-130 kickoff); run rows are the cycle's own and all count
    14	#   --runs FILE…   run-row files (JSONL, `cost_usd` per row); repeatable, and every
    15	#                  following non-option argument is a file too. Default:
    16	#                  grimoires/loa/reports/ablation-2.0/runs.jsonl plus every
    17	#                  evals/results/ablation-2.0/*/rows.jsonl that exists. A row whose
    18	#                  run_id was already counted from another file is counted once.
    19	#   --ledger FILE  cost ledger (JSONL, `ts`, `cost_micro_usd`; default .run/cost-ledger.jsonl)
    20	#   --cap USD      cycle cap (default: evals.ablation.cycle_cap_usd in .loa.config.yaml,
    21	#                  else caps.cycle_usd in evals/suites/ablation-2.0.yaml, else 1500)
    22	#   --reserve USD  reserve (default caps.reserve_usd in the suite file, else 250)
    23	#   --json         one JSON object: total_usd, runs_usd, ledger_usd, since, cap_usd,
    24	#                  headroom_usd, reserve_usd, runs_files, ledger_file, runs_rows,
    25	#                  runs_rows_deduped, ledger_rows, skipped_lines
    26	#
    27	# Output: cycle spend USD T (runs R + ledger L since S); cap C; headroom H; reserve V
    28	#   headroom = cap - total (negative when over). Default files that do not exist
    29	#   count as zero; a malformed line is skipped and counted (stderr note).
    30	#
    31	# Exit: 0 printed; 1 a named file (or an existing default) is unreadable; 2 usage.
    32	# Tested by evals/tests/spend.bats.
    33	# =============================================================================
    34	set -euo pipefail
    35	export LC_ALL=C
    36	
    37	SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
    38	REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)"
    39	SINCE="2026-10-14T13:50:00Z"
    40	LEDGER="" CAP="" RESERVE="" JSON=false
    41	RUNS=()
    42	
    43	usage() { sed -n '2,/^# =====.*$/p' "$0" | sed -n '2,32p' | sed 's/^# \{0,1\}//' >&2; exit 2; }
    44	die() { echo "spend: $*" >&2; exit 2; }
    45	num_ok() { [[ "$1" =~ ^[0-9]+(\.[0-9]+)?$ ]]; }
    46	
    47	while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
    48	  case "$1" in
    49	    --since) SINCE="${2:-}"; shift 2 ;;
    50	    --runs)
    51	      [[ -n "${2:-}" && "${2:-}" != --* ]] || die "--runs needs at least one file"
    52	      shift
    53	      while [[ $# -gt 0 && "$1" != --* ]]; do RUNS+=("$1"); shift; done ;;
    54	    --ledger) LEDGER="${2:-}"; [[ -n "$LEDGER" ]] || die "--ledger needs a file"; shift 2 ;;
    55	    --cap) CAP="${2:-}"; shift 2 ;;
    56	    --reserve) RESERVE="${2:-}"; shift 2 ;;
    57	    --json) JSON=true; shift ;;
    58	    --help|-h) usage ;;
    59	    *) die "unknown option: $1 (see --help)" ;;
    60	  esac
    61	done
    62	[[ "$SINCE" =~ ^[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}(T[0-9]{2}:[0-9]{2}(:[0-9]{2}(\.[0-9]+)?)?(Z|[+-][0-9]{2}:[0-9]{2})?)?$ ]] \
    63	  || die "--since must be an ISO-8601 timestamp (e.g. 2026-10-14T13:50:00Z)"
    64	command -v python3 >/dev/null 2>&1 || die "missing tool: python3"
    65	
    66	SUITE="$REPO_ROOT/evals/suites/ablation-2.0.yaml"
    67	yq_num() {  # yq_num <expr> <file> — a number or empty
    68	  local v
    69	  [[ -f "$2" ]] && command -v yq >/dev/null 2>&1 || return 0
    70	  v="$(yq -r "$1 // \"\"" "$2" 2>/dev/null || true)"
    71	  num_ok "$v" && printf '%s' "$v"
    72	  return 0
    73	}
    74	if [[ -z "$CAP" ]]; then
    75	  CAP="$(yq_num '.evals.ablation.cycle_cap_usd' "$REPO_ROOT/.loa.config.yaml")"
    76	  [[ -n "$CAP" ]] || CAP="$(yq_num '.caps.cycle_usd' "$SUITE")"
    77	  [[ -n "$CAP" ]] || CAP=1500
    78	fi
    79	if [[ -z "$RESERVE" ]]; then
    80	  RESERVE="$(yq_num '.caps.reserve_usd' "$SUITE")"
    81	  [[ -n "$RESERVE" ]] || RESERVE=250
    82	fi
    83	num_ok "$CAP" || die "--cap must be a non-negative number"
    84	num_ok "$RESERVE" || die "--reserve must be a non-negative number"
    85	
    86	# Explicit files must be readable; defaults are optional (absent = zero).
    87	if [[ ${#RUNS[@]} -eq 0 ]]; then
    88	  [[ -e "$REPO_ROOT/grimoires/loa/reports/ablation-2.0/runs.jsonl" ]] && RUNS+=("$REPO_ROOT/grimoires/loa/reports/ablation-2.0/runs.jsonl")
    89	  for f in "$REPO_ROOT"/evals/results/ablation-2.0/*/rows.jsonl; do [[ -e "$f" ]] && RUNS+=("$f"); done
    90	fi
    91	EXPLICIT_LEDGER=true
    92	if [[ -z "$LEDGER" ]]; then
    93	  EXPLICIT_LEDGER=false
    94	  LEDGER="$REPO_ROOT/.run/cost-ledger.jsonl"
    95	fi
    96	for f in ${RUNS[@]+"${RUNS[@]}"}; do
    97	  [[ -f "$f" && -r "$f" ]] || { echo "spend: run-row file unreadable: $f" >&2; exit 1; }
    98	done
    99	if [[ -e "$LEDGER" || "$EXPLICIT_LEDGER" == "true" ]]; then
   100	  [[ -f "$LEDGER" && -r "$LEDGER" ]] || { echo "spend: ledger unreadable: $LEDGER" >&2; exit 1; }
   101	else
   102	  LEDGER=""
   103	fi
   104	
   105	python3 -I - "$SINCE" "$CAP" "$RESERVE" "$JSON" "$LEDGER" ${RUNS[@]+"${RUNS[@]}"} <<'PY'
   106	import json, sys
   107	from datetime import datetime, timezone
   108	
   109	since_s, cap, reserve, as_json, ledger = sys.argv[1], float(sys.argv[2]), float(sys.argv[3]), sys.argv[4] == "true", sys.argv[5]
   110	runs_files = sys.argv[6:]
   111	
   112	def ts(s):
   113	    s = s.strip()
   114	    if len(s) == 10:
   115	        s += "T00:00:00Z"
   116	    d = datetime.fromisoformat(s.replace("Z", "+00:00"))
   117	    return d if d.tzinfo else d.replace(tzinfo=timezone.utc)
   118	
   119	since = ts(since_s)
   120	skipped = 0
   121	runs_usd, runs_rows, dedup = 0.0, 0, 0
   122	seen = set()
   123	for f in runs_files:
   124	    for line in open(f, encoding="utf-8", errors="replace"):
   125	        if not line.strip():
   126	            continue
   127	        try:
   128	            r = json.loads(line)
   129	            c = float(r.get("cost_usd") or 0)
   130	        except (ValueError, TypeError, AttributeError):
   131	            skipped += 1
   132	            continue
   133	        rid = r.get("run_id")
   134	        key = rid if isinstance(rid, str) and rid else None
   135	        if key is not None and key in seen:
   136	            dedup += 1
   137	            continue
   138	        if key is not None:
   139	            seen.add(key)
   140	        runs_usd += c
   141	        runs_rows += 1
   142	
   143	ledger_usd, ledger_rows = 0.0, 0
   144	if ledger:
   145	    for line in open(ledger, encoding="utf-8", errors="replace"):
   146	        if not line.strip():
   147	            continue
   148	        try:
   149	            r = json.loads(line)
   150	            if ts(str(r["ts"])) < since:
   151	                continue
   152	            ledger_usd += float(r.get("cost_micro_usd") or 0) / 1e6
   153	            ledger_rows += 1
   154	        except (ValueError, TypeError, KeyError, AttributeError):
   155	            skipped += 1
   156	
   157	total = runs_usd + ledger_usd
   158	headroom = cap - total
   159	if skipped:
   160	    print(f"spend: skipped {skipped} malformed line(s)", file=sys.stderr)
   161	def n(x):
   162	    x = round(x, 4)
   163	    return int(x) if x == int(x) else x
   164	if as_json:
   165	    print(json.dumps({
   166	        "total_usd": n(total), "runs_usd": n(runs_usd), "ledger_usd": n(ledger_usd),
   167	        "since": since_s, "cap_usd": n(cap), "headroom_usd": n(headroom), "reserve_usd": n(reserve),
   168	        "runs_files": runs_files, "ledger_file": ledger or None, "runs_rows": runs_rows,
   169	        "runs_rows_deduped": dedup, "ledger_rows": ledger_rows, "skipped_lines": skipped}, sort_keys=True))
   170	else:
   171	    def money(x): return f"{x:,.2f}"
   172	    def whole(x): return f"{x:,.0f}" if x == int(x) else f"{x:,.2f}"
   173	    print(f"cycle spend USD {money(total)} (runs {money(runs_usd)} + ledger {money(ledger_usd)} since {since_s}); "
   174	          f"cap {whole(cap)}; headroom {money(headroom)}; reserve {whole(reserve)}")
   175	PY

     3	# validate-suite.sh — cycle-130 ablation task-suite validator (SDD §3.2, DEC-0424)
     4	#
     5	# Checks every task of the ablation-2.0 suite before it is frozen, run or graded.
     6	#
     7	# Usage:
     8	#   validate-suite.sh [--root DIR] [--smoke] [--allow-partial] [--suite-file F]
     9	#
    10	#   --root DIR        suite root (default grimoires/loa/evals/ablation-2.0); the
    11	#                     tasks are <root>/tasks/<id>/task.yaml
    12	#   --smoke           also validate <root>/smoke/<id>/task.yaml (never counted)
    13	#   --allow-partial   skip the four-by-four type count (Sprint 258 state)
    14	#   --suite-file F    suite yaml (default evals/suites/ablation-2.0.yaml): arm ids

   157	def leak_scan(tid, label, text, stems, defect_ids):

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
     2	# =============================================================================
     3	# freeze.sh — cycle-130 ablation suite freeze (SDD §5.13, DEC-0404, DEC-0414)
     4	#
     5	# Writes or verifies <root>/MANIFEST.sha256, the suite's frozen identity: one
     6	# "<sha256>  <relpath>" line per file under <root>/tasks/ (and <root>/smoke/
     7	# with --smoke), relpath relative to the root, LC_ALL=C sorted, sha256 (Python
     8	# hashlib: no harness script sources .claude/ code, eval.yml trust boundary).
     9	# validate-suite.sh runs first; an invalid suite is never frozen or accepted.
    10	#
    11	# Usage:
    12	#   freeze.sh [--root DIR] [--smoke] [--check] [--allow-partial] [--suite-file F]
    13	#
    14	#   --root DIR        suite root (default grimoires/loa/evals/ablation-2.0)
    15	#   --smoke           cover smoke/ too (passed to the validator as well)
    16	#   --check           recompute and compare with MANIFEST.sha256; write nothing
    17	#   --allow-partial   passed to validate-suite.sh (fewer than four tasks per type)
    18	#   --suite-file F    passed to validate-suite.sh
    19	#
    20	# Output: `freeze: wrote MANIFEST.sha256 (N files, sha256 <digest of the manifest>)`
    21	# or `freeze: OK — N files match MANIFEST.sha256 (sha256 …)`; on drift every
    22	# changed / added / removed path on its own line.
    23	#
    24	# Exit: 0 written / matches; 1 drift, missing manifest under --check, or the
    25	#       validator found violations; 2 usage.
    26	# Tested by evals/tests/freeze.bats.
    27	# =============================================================================
    28	set -euo pipefail

  mkdir -p "$dest"

# Parent-side: append a finished job's row and update the counters.
collect() {  # collect <job-id> <arm>
  local jid="$1" arm="$2" i
  i="$(arm_index "$arm")"
  if [[ -f "$JOBS_DIR/$jid.flag" ]]; then
    log "corpus drift before $jid: $(cat "$JOBS_DIR/$jid.drift" 2>/dev/null)"
    set_state failed; exit 3
  fi
  if [[ -f "$JOBS_DIR/$jid.row" ]]; then
    mkdir -p "$BATCH_DIR/$arm"
    cat "$JOBS_DIR/$jid.row" >> "$BATCH_DIR/$arm/results.jsonl"
    local cost
    cost="$(jq -r '(.executor.total_cost_usd // 0) | tonumber? // 0' "$JOBS_DIR/$jid.row" 2>/dev/null || echo 0)"
    [[ "$cost" =~ ^[0-9]+(\.[0-9]+)?([eE][-+]?[0-9]+)?$ ]] || cost=0
    SPENT="$(fadd "$SPENT" "$cost")"
    if [[ "$(jq -r '.status' "$JOBS_DIR/$jid.row")" == "completed" ]]; then
      ARM_SUM[$i]="$(fadd "${ARM_SUM[$i]}" "$cost")"; ARM_N[$i]=$(( ${ARM_N[$i]} + 1 ))
      POOL_SUM="$(fadd "$POOL_SUM" "$cost")"; POOL_N=$((POOL_N + 1))
    fi
    if [[ "$(jq -r '.status' "$JOBS_DIR/$jid.row")" == "completed" ]]; then
      DONE[$i]=$(( ${DONE[$i]} + 1 ))
      log "done $jid ($(jq -r '"\(.arm) \(.fixture) t\(.trial) recall=\(([.graders[]? | select(.name=="recall-vs-defects.sh") | .details.recall][0]) // "n/a") \(.duration_ms/1000|floor)s"' "$JOBS_DIR/$jid.row"))"
    else
      FAILED[$i]=$(( ${FAILED[$i]} + 1 ))
      log "FAILED $jid ($(jq -c '.error' "$JOBS_DIR/$jid.row"))"
    fi
    rm -f "$JOBS_DIR/$jid".*
  else
    FAILED[$i]=$(( ${FAILED[$i]} + 1 ))
    log "FAILED $jid (no row written; see $JOBS_DIR/$jid.exec.log)"
  fi
  write_status
}

#!/usr/bin/env bats
# =============================================================================
# evals/tests/took-effect.bats — cycle-130 Sprint 258 Task 1.8 (SDD D-4.2, §5.10; AC-1.8)
#
# evals/harness/took-effect.sh evaluates each arm's `took_effect` rule ids against
# a run directory's artefacts. Every rule gets a passing case (the arm's own fixture
# run) and a failing case (another arm's run judged under this arm, or a mutated
# copy). Fixtures: evals/tests/fixtures/ablation-runs/ (regen.sh rebuilds them).
# =============================================================================

setup() {
  TESTS_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "$BATS_TEST_FILENAME")" && pwd)"
  REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$TESTS_DIR/../.." && pwd)"
  TE="$REPO_ROOT/evals/harness/took-effect.sh"
  FX="$TESTS_DIR/fixtures/ablation-runs"
  SUITE="$FX/suite.yaml"
  T="$(mktemp -d "${BATS_TEST_TMPDIR:-/tmp}/te.XXXXXX")"
  cp -a "$FX/runs" "$T/runs"
}

teardown() {
  find "$T" -mindepth 1 -delete 2>/dev/null || true
  rmdir "$T" 2>/dev/null || true
}

te() {  # te <run> [--arm ID] [--json]
  local run="$1"; shift
  run "$TE" --run-dir "$T/runs/$run" --suite-file "$SUITE" "$@"
}
line() { printf '%s\n' "$output" | grep -E "^arm [a-z0-9_]+: $1 " ; }   # the rule's line
edit_json() { jq "$2" "$1" > "$T/x.json" && mv "$T/x.json" "$1"; }

@test "every fixture run passes its own arm's rules (exit 0, final OK line)" {
  local r
  for r in a0-build a1-build a1-review a2-build a3-review a4-build a5-build a6-build a7-build refused-a4-review; do
    te "$r"
    [ "$status" -eq 0 ] || { echo "$r: $output"; return 1; }
    [[ "$(printf '%s\n' "$output" | sed -n '$p')" =~ ^arm\ [a-z0-9_]+:\ OK$ ]]
  done
}

#!/usr/bin/env bats
# =============================================================================
# evals/tests/took-effect.bats — cycle-130 Sprint 258 Task 1.8 (SDD D-4.2, §5.10; AC-1.8)
#
# evals/harness/took-effect.sh evaluates each arm's `took_effect` rule ids against
# a run directory's artefacts. Every rule gets a passing case (the arm's own fixture
# run) and a failing case (another arm's run judged under this arm, or a mutated
# copy). Fixtures: evals/tests/fixtures/ablation-runs/ (regen.sh rebuilds them).
# =============================================================================

setup() {
  TESTS_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "$BATS_TEST_FILENAME")" && pwd)"
  REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$TESTS_DIR/../.." && pwd)"
  TE="$REPO_ROOT/evals/harness/took-effect.sh"
  FX="$TESTS_DIR/fixtures/ablation-runs"
  SUITE="$FX/suite.yaml"
  T="$(mktemp -d "${BATS_TEST_TMPDIR:-/tmp}/te.XXXXXX")"
  cp -a "$FX/runs" "$T/runs"
}

teardown() {
  find "$T" -mindepth 1 -delete 2>/dev/null || true
  rmdir "$T" 2>/dev/null || true
}

te() {  # te <run> [--arm ID] [--json]
  local run="$1"; shift
  run "$TE" --run-dir "$T/runs/$run" --suite-file "$SUITE" "$@"
}
line() { printf '%s\n' "$output" | grep -E "^arm [a-z0-9_]+: $1 " ; }   # the rule's line
edit_json() { jq "$2" "$1" > "$T/x.json" && mv "$T/x.json" "$1"; }

@test "every fixture run passes its own arm's rules (exit 0, final OK line)" {
  local r
  for r in a0-build a1-build a1-review a2-build a3-review a4-build a5-build a6-build a7-build refused-a4-review; do
    te "$r"
    [ "$status" -eq 0 ] || { echo "$r: $output"; return 1; }
    [[ "$(printf '%s\n' "$output" | sed -n '$p')" =~ ^arm\ [a-z0-9_]+:\ OK$ ]]
  done
}

== spend
1..6
not ok 1 SP-1 rows (deduplicated by run_id) plus ledger rows since the default kickoff: the summary line

not ok 5 SP-5 exit 1 on an unreadable file; exit 2 on usage errors
not ok 6 SP-6 the default cap and reserve come from the suite file's caps block (1500, 250)
== freeze
1..6
not ok 1 FZ-1 freeze writes one sorted '<sha256>  <relpath>' line per file under tasks/; --check then passes
not ok 2 FZ-2 one changed byte under tasks/ is drift: --check exits 1 and names the path; added and removed files too
not ok 3 FZ-3 an invalid suite is never frozen: exit 1, no manifest written
not ok 4 FZ-4 --smoke covers smoke/; without it smoke files are outside the manifest
not ok 5 FZ-5 --check without a manifest is exit 1; usage errors are exit 2
not ok 6 FZ-6 the committed suite root's MANIFEST.sha256 matches its smoke tasks
== validate-suite
1..10
not ok 1 VS-1 the committed smoke tasks validate (--smoke --allow-partial); without --allow-partial the empty tasks/ fails the counts
not ok 2 VS-2 a four-by-four suite validates; one task short fails the counts unless --allow-partial; smoke tasks never count
not ok 3 VS-3 leakage: 'hidden', a hidden test stem, an arm id or a defect key in TASK.md, and a path in the criterion, are each listed
not ok 4 VS-4 leakage in a phase prompt is listed for every task
not ok 5 VS-5 allowlist: a test_command or regression_command outside python3|pytest|bats|bash|node|npx is refused
not ok 6 VS-6 hidden/manifest.json: a '..' dest, an absolute dest, a missing src and a mount-owned dest are refused
not ok 7 VS-7 fixture path rule: a fixture holding .claude/ or grimoires/, or a reference patch touching .claude/, is refused
not ok 8 VS-8 schema: a missing field, an unknown type, a suite_version mismatch, a review-catch without review_catch and a refactor without structural_check are all listed
not ok 9 VS-9 suite file: an arm whose task_types names an unknown type is refused; the committed suite file passes
not ok 10 VS-10 usage: an unknown option, a missing root or suite file is exit 2

1..52

ok 2 dry-run: A0 is one BARE phase with --max-turns 170 and the summed 70-minute timeout
ok 3 dry-run: BARE without a suite declaration is the sum of the implementer caps

not ok 6 A1: only the review gate requests changes → FIX1 runs, FIX2 is skipped

not ok 14 A3: the REVIEW and AUDIT envelopes carry companion_voice.planned false
not ok 15 A5: PLAN runs with the Flatline step off; A1's PLAN prompt has it on
not ok 16 A6: one implementer session across PLAN, IMPLEMENT and FIX with --resume; gates separate
not ok 17 A0: one BARE phase, no .claude/ or CLAUDE.md or grimoire, --effort high, --max-turns 170
not ok 18 A7: --effort medium on every argv and no effort: line left in a sandbox SKILL.md
not ok 19 A1: no --effort flag; effort_requested is the sandbox skill frontmatter
not ok 20 review-catch A1: REVIEW then AUDIT on the PR under pr/, dissent pointed at pr/head.diff
not ok 21 review-catch A0: one BARE phase with the arm-neutral output contract
ok 22 applicability: A4 on a review-catch task is refused (exit 2, meta/refused.json, no phase)
ok 23 applicability: the absent A8 and an undeclared arm are refused
not ok 24 no hidden path in the sandbox; prompts and task-brief carry no hidden, defect key or arm id
ok 25 leak guard: a task-brief naming a defect key is refused before any phase (exit 2)
ok 26 leak guard: an arm id inside the sandbox tree is refused (exit 2)
ok 27 leak guard: a fixture carrying a hidden directory is refused (exit 2)

not ok 29 argv: stream-json, bypassPermissions, --setting-sources project and the fixed tools list on every phase

not ok 32 cwd: every phase runs at the sandbox root
not ok 33 cap: the phase whose result cost passes USD 12 stops the run (cap_failure, cap_phase, exit 3)
not ok 34 cap: sandbox cost-ledger rows written during a phase count toward the cap

not ok 44 meta boundary: the arm id lives under meta/ only — never in sandbox/, snapshots/, transcripts/, eval/
not ok 45 manifest: the sandbox manifest is regenerated after the toggles for every arm

not ok 49 container: the per-run HOME persists across the phases of one run and is deleted when interrupted
not ok 50 bedrock route: the bearer token and route keys reach the CLI (host and container); no artefact carries the token
not ok 51 container: a missing image is an infrastructure error (exit 2); host mode makes no per-run HOME
not ok 52 fingerprint.sh: fp:<sha256> over the tool versions and the source tree HEAD

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
     2	# =============================================================================
     3	# tools/fresh-mount-proof.sh — cycle-130 FR-1 (#1267; SDD §5.4, AC-1.3)
     4	#
     5	# Proves that a FRESH downstream submodule mount of this repository passes
     6	# `check-loa.sh` integrity: no Tampered, no Missing (paths the mount does not
     7	# link by design are reported as not-mounted and do not fail).
     8	#
     9	# Steps, all inside a new temp directory (nothing outside it is written):
    10	#   1. upstream/   — a `git clone` of this repository over file://, with a
    11	#                    local branch `fresh-mount-proof` at REF. With --worktree
    12	#                    the source work tree's uncommitted state (tracked edits,
    13	#                    deletions and untracked non-ignored files) is copied in
    14	#                    and committed on that branch, inside the temp clone only.
    15	#   2. downstream/ — `git init`, one commit, then the downstream entry point
    16	#                    `upstream/.claude/scripts/mount-submodule.sh --branch
    17	#                    fresh-mount-proof --ref <sha> --force` with
    18	#                    LOA_UPSTREAM=file://.../upstream (the mount clones the
    19	#                    submodule from there; no network).
    20	#   3. `aleph.enabled: false` is set in downstream/.loa.config.yaml.
    21	#   4. `bash .claude/scripts/check-loa.sh` runs in downstream/; its full output
    22	#      is printed, then a summary line
    23	#        fresh-mount-proof: Tampered=T Missing=M not-mounted=N check-loa-rc=R
    24	#
    25	# Git runs hermetically: GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null, GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1,
    26	# a fixed identity, protocol.file.allow=always (needed for a file:// submodule
    27	# on git >= 2.38.1) and core.hooksPath pointed at an empty directory.
    28	#
    29	# Usage:
    30	#   tools/fresh-mount-proof.sh [--ref REF] [--worktree] [--keep] [--tmp DIR]
    31	#
    32	# Options:
    33	#   --ref REF    commit-ish of this repository to mount (default: HEAD of the
    34	#                repository the script lives in)
    35	#   --worktree   mount REF plus the source work tree's uncommitted state
    36	#                (use before the change is committed)
    37	#   --keep       keep the temp directory and print its path
    38	#   --tmp DIR    parent directory for the temp directory (default: $TMPDIR or
    39	#                /tmp)
    40	#   -h, --help   this text
    41	#
    42	# Exit codes:
    43	#   0    check-loa.sh exited 0 on the fresh mount
    44	#   1    check-loa.sh exited non-zero (its output names the failures)
    45	#   2    usage error
    46	#   3    setup failed (clone, overlay, downstream init or the mount itself);
    47	#        the failing step's output is printed
    48	# =============================================================================
    49	set -euo pipefail
    50	export LC_ALL=C
    51	
    52	usage() { sed -n '/^# Usage:/,/^# =====/p' "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}" | sed -e '$d' -e 's/^# \{0,1\}//'; }
    53	die2() { echo "fresh-mount-proof: $*" >&2; exit 2; }
    54	die3() { echo "fresh-mount-proof: SETUP FAILED: $*" >&2; exit 3; }
    55	
    56	REF=""
    57	KEEP=0
    58	WORKTREE=0
    59	TMP_PARENT="${TMPDIR:-/tmp}"
    60	while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
    61	  case "$1" in
    62	    --ref)
    63	      [[ $# -ge 2 && -n "$2" ]] || die2 "--ref requires a commit-ish"
    64	      REF="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    65	    --tmp)
    66	      [[ $# -ge 2 && -n "$2" ]] || die2 "--tmp requires a directory"
    67	      TMP_PARENT="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    68	    --keep) KEEP=1; shift ;;
    69	    --worktree) WORKTREE=1; shift ;;
    70	    -h|--help) usage; exit 0 ;;
    71	    *) die2 "unknown argument: $1 (see --help)" ;;
    72	  esac
    73	done
    74	[[ -d "$TMP_PARENT" ]] || die2 "--tmp is not a directory: $TMP_PARENT"
    75	
    76	SELF_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd -P)"
    77	SRC="$(git -C "$SELF_DIR" rev-parse --show-toplevel 2>/dev/null)" || die2 "script is not inside a git work tree"
    78	[[ -n "$REF" ]] || REF="HEAD"
    79	REF_SHA="$(git -C "$SRC" rev-parse --verify --quiet "${REF}^{commit}")" || die2 "not a commit in $SRC: $REF"
    80	
    81	WORK="$(mktemp -d "${TMP_PARENT%/}/fresh-mount-proof.XXXXXX")"
    82	cleanup() {

#!/usr/bin/env bats
# =============================================================================
# evals/tests/pipeline-run.bats — cycle-130 Sprint 258 Tasks 1.7 + 1.12
# (SDD §1.4 D-4.1 … D-4.10, §5.6; sprint.md AC-1.7, AC-1.12, AC-1.14; PRD AC-4.x)
#
# evals/harness/pipeline-run.sh drives Loa's phases as separate CLI sessions in a
# sandbox repository. Here the CLI is evals/tests/fixtures/claude-stub-pipeline.sh,
# docker is fixtures/docker-stub.sh, and the executor runs from a temporary copy of
# the harness (make_harness) whose lib/sandbox-mount.sh is fixtures/mount-lib-stub.sh:
# the shipped script sources its library by a literal path only (eval.yml trust
# boundary), so there is no environment override to point. The executor runs the CLI under
# `env -i`, which strips the stubs' control variables, so each test reaches the
# stubs through generated wrappers ($T/claude, $T/docker) that first record the
# environment and descriptors the executor gave them, then load $T/stub.env.
# =============================================================================

setup() {
  TESTS_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "$BATS_TEST_FILENAME")" && pwd)"
  REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$TESTS_DIR/../.." && pwd)"
  FP="$REPO_ROOT/evals/harness/fingerprint.sh"
  STUB="$TESTS_DIR/fixtures/claude-stub-pipeline.sh"
  DSTUB="$TESTS_DIR/fixtures/docker-stub.sh"
  T="$(mktemp -d "${BATS_TEST_TMPDIR:-/tmp}/pr.XXXXXX")"
  export LOA_EVAL_WATCHDOG_POLL_S=0.1
  export LOA_EVAL_PRICING_JSON='{"global.anthropic.claude-opus-5-5":{"input_per_mtok":4000000,"output_per_mtok":20000000},"global.anthropic.claude-fable-5-1":{"input_per_mtok":10000000,"output_per_mtok":50000000}}'
  export LOA_EVAL_CREDS_HOME="$T/home"
  : > "$T/stub.env"
  make_harness
  make_source_tree
  cp "$TESTS_DIR/fixtures/ablation-runs/suite.yaml" "$T/suite.yaml"   # B's suite file as landed
  make_tasks
  make_wrappers
}

teardown() {
  chmod -R u+rwx "$T" 2>/dev/null || true
  find "$T" -mindepth 1 -delete 2>/dev/null || true
  rmdir "$T" 2>/dev/null || true
}

make_source_tree() {
  local s
  mkdir -p "$T/src/.claude/loa" "$T/src/.claude/scripts"
  for s in planning-sprints implementing-tasks reviewing-code auditing-security; do
    mkdir -p "$T/src/.claude/skills/$s"
    printf -- '---\nname: %s\neffort: xhigh\n---\nbody\n' "$s" > "$T/src/.claude/skills/$s/SKILL.md"
  done
  echo "loa" > "$T/src/.claude/loa/CLAUDE.loa.md"
  printf 'flatline_protocol:\n  enabled: true\n  code_review:\n    enabled: true\n  security_audit:\n    enabled: true\n' > "$T/src/.loa.config.yaml"
  ( cd "$T/src" && git init -q && git add -A && git -c user.email=t@t -c user.name=t commit -qm init )
  # the operator's credential directories (copied per run in container mode)
  mkdir -p "$T/home/.aws" "$T/home/.claude/projects/big" "$T/home/.codex/sessions"
  echo "[default]" > "$T/home/.aws/config"
  echo "{}" > "$T/home/.claude/settings.json"
  echo "history" > "$T/home/.claude/history.jsonl"
  echo "{}" > "$T/home/.codex/auth.json"
  echo "model = 'x'" > "$T/home/.codex/config.toml"
  echo '{"claudeAiOauth": "subscription"}' > "$T/home/.claude/.credentials.json"
}

# a temporary copy of the harness: the stub mount library sits at the literal path
# pipeline-run.sh sources (lib/sandbox-mount.sh)
make_harness() {
  H="$T/h/evals/harness"
  mkdir -p "$H/lib"
  cp "$REPO_ROOT/evals/harness/pipeline-run.sh" "$REPO_ROOT/evals/harness/fingerprint.sh" "$H/"
  cp -a "$REPO_ROOT/evals/harness/lib/phase-prompts" "$H/lib/"
  cp "$TESTS_DIR/fixtures/mount-lib-stub.sh" "$H/lib/sandbox-mount.sh"
  PR="$H/pipeline-run.sh"
}

make_tasks() {
  # build task: fixture tree beside a sibling hidden/ directory that must never be copied
  local b="$T/suite/tasks/bf-01" r="$T/suite/tasks/rc-01" p="$T/prs/pr-x"
  mkdir -p "$b/fx/src" "$b/hidden/tests"
  echo 'print(1)' > "$b/fx/src/app.py"
  echo 'assert False' > "$b/hidden/tests/test_secret.py"
  printf 'Make the app print two.\n' > "$b/TASK.md"
  cat > "$b/task.yaml" <<'YAML'
id: bf-01
schema_version: 1
type: bug-fix
fixture: fx
criterion: "the app prints two"
test_command: ["python3", "-m", "pytest", "-q", "tests"]
YAML
  # review-catch task: a PR fixture outside the task dir
  mkdir -p "$p/base/lib" "$p/head/lib" "$r"
  echo 'a=1' > "$p/base/lib/x.sh"; echo 'a=2' > "$p/head/lib/x.sh"
  printf -- '--- a/lib/x.sh\n+++ b/lib/x.sh\n@@ -1 +1 @@\n-a=1\n+a=2\n' > "$p/head.diff"
  printf '# PR\nChange a.\n' > "$p/PR.md"
  printf '# Review instructions\nReview it.\n' > "$p/REVIEW-INSTRUCTIONS.md"
  printf '# Audit instructions\nAudit it.\n' > "$p/AUDIT-INSTRUCTIONS.md"
  printf 'name: pr-x\ndescription: "planted defects live elsewhere"\n' > "$p/fixture.yaml"
  printf 'Review the pull request in pr/.\n' > "$r/TASK.md"
  cat > "$r/task.yaml" <<YAML
id: rc-01
schema_version: 1
type: review-catch
fixture: null
criterion: "review the change"
review_catch: {fixture: "$p"}
YAML
  BUILD="$b/task.yaml" REVIEWC="$r/task.yaml"
}

make_wrappers() {
  mkdir -p "$T/log" "$T/dlog"
  cat > "$T/claude" <<EOF
#!/usr/bin/env bash
env | sed -E 's/^(AWS_BEARER_TOKEN_BEDROCK)=.*/\1=<set>/' > "$T/log/pending.env"   # key name only, never the value
if [[ -n "\${AWS_BEARER_TOKEN_BEDROCK:-}" ]]; then
  if [[ "\$AWS_BEARER_TOKEN_BEDROCK" == "\$(cat "$T/token" 2>/dev/null)" ]]; then echo match; else echo mismatch; fi >> "$T/log/token.check"
fi
ls "/proc/\$\$/fd" > "$T/log/pending.fds" 2>/dev/null || true
set -a; . "$T/stub.env"; set +a
export STUB_LOG_DIR="$T/log"
exec "$STUB" "\$@"
EOF
  cat > "$T/docker" <<EOF
#!/usr/bin/env bash
export DOCKER_STUB_LOG="$T/dlog" DOCKER_STUB_CLAUDE="$T/claude"
[[ -f "$T/docker.env" ]] && { set -a; . "$T/docker.env"; set +a; }
exec "$DSTUB" "\$@"
EOF
  chmod +x "$T/claude" "$T/docker"
}

# run_pr <arm> [task-yaml] [extra args…] — host executor unless --executor given
run_pr() {
  local arm="$1" task="${2:-$BUILD}"; shift; [[ $# -gt 0 ]] && shift
  run "$PR" --task-yaml "$task" --arm "$arm" --run-dir "$T/run" --run-id "r-$arm" --trial 1 \
    --source-tree "$T/src" --suite-file "$T/suite.yaml" --executor host --claude-bin "$T/claude" "$@"
}
labels() { jq -r '[.phases[] | .label] | join(",")' "$T/run/meta/pipeline.json"; }
ran()    { jq -r '[.phases[] | select(.skipped == false) | .label] | join(",")' "$T/run/meta/pipeline.json"; }
argv_of() { tr '\0' '\n' < "$T/log/call-$1.argv"; }   # argv_of <n>
call_for() { grep -lx "$1" "$T"/log/call-*.phase | sed -n '1p' | sed 's/.*call-\([0-9]*\)\.phase/\1/'; }

content.text:
This PR can't merge: I wrote 14 findings to `/workspace/review.md`, and the verdict is **CHANGES_REQUIRED**. Nothing under `pr/` was changed.

**Blocking:**
- **The new CI gates fail as soon as they land.** The PR edits several tracked `.claude/` files (model-config.yaml, check-loa.sh, preflight.sh, generated-model-maps.sh, CLAUDE.loa.md, the bridgebuilder files) but doesn't regenerate or commit `.claude/checksums.json`. So the new `gen-checksums.sh --check` step reports drift on every edited file. The #1267 fix also never regenerates the old manifest it was meant to clean up.
- **The CI path filters weren't extended.** They don't cover `evals/**`, the new `tools/` scripts or most of `.claude/skills/**`. The new eval-harness test step and the manifest gate never run on a PR that touches only those paths.
- **Two test files fail on a clean checkout.** `took-effect.bats` and `ablation-row.bats` copy `fixtures/ablation-runs/runs/`, which the PR doesn't commit. After I generated it with the PR's `regen.sh`, all 39 cases passed.
- **jq 1.6 breaks the pipeline.** `pipeline-run.sh`, `ablation-row.sh` and `sandbox-mount.sh` use `label` as a jq variable or key, which jq 1.6 rejects. jq 1.6 is the stock package on Debian 12 and Ubuntu 22.04. I reproduced the failure under 1.6 and saw it pass under 1.7.1. CI (ubuntu-latest) has 1.7.1, so it won't catch this.
- **Secrets reach untrusted code.** `init_sandbox_beads` runs a `.claude/` script from the tree under test with the driver's full environment, including `AWS_BEARER_TOKEN_BEDROCK`. That breaks the trust boundary the harness says it keeps. `price_for` also runs the checkout's `.claude/` `pricing.py`.

**Experiment validity:**
- The A0 (no-mount) prompt omits the task's `criterion`, which every other arm receives. The A0-vs-A1 comparison therefore also changes how much task information the agent gets.
- `took-effect.sh` fails A3 and A6 runs that stopped early for ordinary reasons (spend cap, agent error). The suite counts such a failure as an infrastructure error and pauses the arm.

**Lower severity:**
- A Dockerfile build stage that can't succeed and is never used.
- A version mismatch: the `pipeline-run.sh` header says codex 0.137.0, the Dockerfile pins 0.162.1.
- A fallback bats path hard-coded to one operator's home directory.
- `check-manifest-paths.sh` lists files in quoted form, so paths with special characters are flagged as untracked.
- `preflight.sh` counts files differently from `gen-checksums.sh`.

**How I tested:** I ran the PR's own test suites from a copy outside `pr/`, using a jq 1.7.1 binary downloaded to `~/bin`.
- **Pass:** the spend tests and every non-container pipeline-run case.
- **Container cases (5):** they failed here only because the docker stub mistakes test paths under `/home/evaluser` for the container's home directory. I'm not counting that as a PR defect.
- **Not verifiable here:** the arm-toggles, run-arms, freeze, validate-suite and `tests/unit` suites need repository files that aren't part of this PR.

- **Two test files fail on a clean checkout.** `took-effect.bats` and `ablation-row.bats` copy `fixtures/ablation-runs/runs/`, which the PR doesn't commit. After I generated it with the PR's `regen.sh`, all 39 cases passed.
- **jq 1.6 breaks the pipeline.** `pipeline-run.sh`, `ablation-row.sh` and `sandbox-mount.sh` use `label` as a jq variable or key, which jq 1.6 rejects. jq 1.6 is the stock package on Debian 12 and Ubuntu 22.04. I reproduced the failure under 1.6 and saw it pass under 1.7.1. CI (ubuntu-latest) has 1.7.1, so it won't catch this.
- **Secrets reach untrusted code.** `init_sandbox_beads` runs a `.claude/` script from the tree under test with the driver's full environment, including `AWS_BEARER_TOKEN_BEDROCK`. That breaks the trust boundary the harness says it keeps. `price_for` also runs the checkout's `.claude/` `pricing.py`.

**Experiment validity:**
- The A0 (no-mount) prompt omits the task's `criterion`, which every other arm receives. The A0-vs-A1 comparison therefore also changes how much task information the agent gets.
- `took-effect.sh` fails A3 and A6 runs that stopped early for ordinary reasons (spend cap, agent error). The suite counts such a failure as an infrastructure error and pauses the arm.

**Lower severity:**
- A Dockerfile build stage that can't succeed and is never used.
- A version mismatch: the `pipeline-run.sh` header says codex 0.137.0, the Dockerfile pins 0.162.1.
- A fallback bats path hard-coded to one operator's home directory.
- `check-manifest-paths.sh` lists files in quoted form, so paths with special characters are flagged as untracked.
- `preflight.sh` counts files differently from `gen-checksums.sh`.

**How I tested:** I ran the PR's own test suites from a copy outside `pr/`, using a jq 1.7.1 binary downloaded to `~/bin`.
- **Pass:** the spend tests and every non-container pipeline-run case.
- **Container cases (5):** they failed here only because the docker stub mistakes test paths under `/home/evaluser` for the container's home directory. I'm not counting that as a PR defect.
- **Not verifiable here:** the arm-toggles, run-arms, freeze, validate-suite and `tests/unit` suites need repository files that aren't part of this PR.
